    input joined the conversation, say, for a provider that sends no acknowledgement to report it in. (An
    [`InferredLifecycle`][pydantic_ai.realtime.lifecycle.InferredLifecycle] has them in
    [`take_pending`][pydantic_ai.realtime.lifecycle.InferredLifecycle.take_pending].)

    Concrete connections accept provider-specific data and control inputs. OpenAI accepts audio,
    text, images, tool results, manual turn controls, cancellation, and truncation; Gemini accepts
    audio, text, images, and tool results. A high-level
    [`RealtimeSession`][pydantic_ai.realtime.RealtimeSession] checks profile-gated operations and
    raises [`UserError`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.UserError], as does a connection handed an input it
    can't send.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

items.title: frames abstractmethod
items.text:
frames()

Iterate over what the model does, a RealtimeFrame at a time.

Each frame holds the codec events one message from the provider makes, in order, with the lifecycle events about them, and ends once the connection is gone for good: by then every response it started has ended (as 'lost' if nothing else ended it). A protocol that identifies nothing itself can have an InferredLifecycle make its frames.

def frames(self) -> AsyncIterator[RealtimeFrame]:
    """Iterate over what the model does, a [`RealtimeFrame`][pydantic_ai.realtime.lifecycle.RealtimeFrame] at a time.

    Each frame holds the codec events one message from the provider makes, in order, with the
    [lifecycle events][pydantic_ai.realtime.lifecycle] about them, and ends once the connection is gone for
    good: by then every response it started has ended (as `'lost'` if nothing else ended it). A protocol
    that identifies nothing itself can have an
    [`InferredLifecycle`][pydantic_ai.realtime.lifecycle.InferredLifecycle] make its frames.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

items.title: set_message_history
items.text:
set_message_history(message_history)

Tell the connection how to read the message history as it currently stands.

A RealtimeSession calls this when it takes ownership of the connection, so a provider that loses server-side state on reconnect can replay the conversation into the new session instead of resuming with total amnesia. The session's history grows as the call goes on, hence a callable rather than a snapshot.

A no-op by default: a provider with native session resumption (Gemini Live) has nothing to replay, and one that can't seed a session at all has nowhere to put it.

    """Tell the connection how to read the message history as it currently stands.

    the connection, so a provider that loses server-side state on

    session instead of resuming with total amnesia. The session's history grows as the call goes on,
    hence a callable rather than a snapshot.

    A no-op by default: a provider with native session resumption (Gemini Live) has nothing to
    replay, and one that can't seed a session at all has nowhere to put it.
    """

items.title: merge_realtime_profile
items.text:
merge_realtime_profile(base, *overrides)

Merge realtime profiles, with later layers overriding earlier ones.

Source code in pydantic_ai/realtime/profiles.py 
def merge_realtime_profile(
    base: RealtimeModelProfile | None, *overrides: RealtimeModelProfile | None
) -> RealtimeModelProfile:
    """Merge realtime profiles, with later layers overriding earlier ones."""
    resolved: RealtimeModelProfile = {}
    if base:
        resolved.update(base)
    for override in overrides:
        if override:
            resolved.update(override)
    return resolved

🌐 এই পেজের সহজ বাংলা সংস্করণ এখনো তৈরি হচ্ছে

আপাতত নিচে মূল ইংরেজি লেখাটি দেখানো হচ্ছে। এই অংশের অন্য পেজগুলোতে সহজ বাংলা ব্যাখ্যা পাবেন।

অফিসিয়াল ইংরেজি পেজ

The ElevenLabs realtime provider, for the Eleven Realtime speech-to-speech models. Requires the elevenlabs-realtime optional group (pip install "pydantic-ai-slim[elevenlabs-realtime]"), which includes openai because the model reuses the OpenAI Realtime codec, whose event types come from the OpenAI SDK.

ElevenLabsRealtimeModel is an OpenAIRealtimeModel pointed at ElevenLabs, authenticated by the same ElevenLabsProvider as ElevenLabs Agents. For a hosted ElevenLabs agent, use ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModel instead.

items.title: pydantic_ai.realtime.elevenlabs
items.text:
ElevenLabs realtime API provider for Eleven Realtime speech-to-speech sessions.

Connects to wss://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/realtime over a WebSocket. Eleven Realtime speaks the OpenAI Realtime protocol, so ElevenLabsRealtimeModel is an OpenAIRealtimeModel pointed at ElevenLabs: it reuses the OpenAI codec (event mapping, session seeding, tool conversion, reconnect-by-replay, and the WebSocket connection itself), authenticated with the key and base URL of the shared ElevenLabsProvider, and diverges only where ElevenLabs does:

  • authentication uses the xi-api-key header, and the model is chosen with session.model in session.update (the server ignores OpenAI's ?model= query parameter);
  • turn detection is semantic VAD only: the server rejects server_vad, so the cross-provider turn_detection setting maps onto semantic VAD;
  • input transcription is always on, even with input_transcription_model=None, and takes no model, only a language (see elevenlabs_language);
  • voices are ElevenLabs voices, set with elevenlabs_voice;
  • response.done carries no usage, so sessions report no token counts;
  • conversation.item.delete is not implemented, so openai_prune_tool_items is ignored;
  • images are dropped from user messages, and seeded history can only carry text;
  • text output (output_modalities: ['text']) ignores audio input altogether, so output_modality='text' is unsupported;
  • the server ends a session after max_duration_seconds (600 by default; see elevenlabs_max_duration_seconds) or after 60 seconds without a client message. With a reconnect policy, either close is re-dialed and the local message history replayed into a new session.

WebRTC is not supported, as ElevenLabs serves no /realtime/calls endpoint, but create_client_secret mints the ephemeral credential a browser uses to open the WebSocket directly.

For a hosted ElevenLabs agent, use ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModel instead.

Requires the websockets package (the realtime optional group) and openai (the openai group, whose SDK supplies the event types the shared OpenAI codec is built on):

pip install "pydantic-ai-slim[elevenlabs-realtime]"

items.title: ElevenLabsRealtimeModelSettings
items.text:
Bases: OpenAIRealtimeModelSettings

Settings specific to Eleven Realtime models.

This inherits every OpenAIRealtimeModelSettings field, since the session is configured with OpenAI's session.update shape. openai_turn_detection is sent as on OpenAI, except that ElevenLabs only supports semantic VAD: a ServerVAD value raises a UserError.

The remaining inherited fields are silently ignored, because ElevenLabs accepts and then drops them: openai_voice (ElevenLabs voices are set with elevenlabs_voice), openai_input_noise_reduction, openai_output_speed, openai_truncation, and openai_prune_tool_items and openai_keep_tool_items (the server doesn't implement conversation.item.delete). So are the shared parallel_tool_calls and thinking settings. Input audio is always transcribed: input_transcription_model takes 'auto' (the default) or None, which still leaves transcripts on, and any other value raises a UserError.

items.title: elevenlabs_voice instance-attribute
items.text:
elevenlabs_voice

Voice used for audio output: an ElevenLabs voice ID (e.g. 'JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb') or the name of a default voice. The server's default is 'brian'.

items.title: elevenlabs_language instance-attribute
items.text:
elevenlabs_language

Language code of the conversation (e.g. 'en', 'es', 'pt-br'), used for transcription, speech, and the model's reply language. The server's default is English.

items.title: elevenlabs_strip_audio_tags instance-attribute
items.text:
elevenlabs_strip_audio_tags

Whether to remove expressive audio tags such as [cheerful] from the model's transcripts. Defaults to True.

Eleven Realtime writes tags into its reply to direct the delivery, and they are part of the transcript, though they aren't spoken. They are removed from the transcript, streamed and in history alike, and the tags a response's transcript held are kept, in order and without brackets, in its provider_details['audio_tags']. Only lowercase words in square brackets count as tags, so citations ([1]), Markdown links, and placeholders like [Your Name] are kept. Set this to False to keep the transcript exactly as ElevenLabs sends it, tags included.

items.title: elevenlabs_max_duration_seconds instance-attribute
items.text:
elevenlabs_max_duration_seconds

Maximum wall-clock duration of a session, in seconds, from 60 to 7200. The server's default is 600.

The server closes the WebSocket once it is exceeded. With a reconnect policy, the session carries on over a new connection, with the local message history replayed into it.

Bases: OpenAIRealtimeConnection

A live WebSocket connection to the ElevenLabs realtime API.

Reuses OpenAIRealtimeConnection for the shared wire protocol, including reconnecting by replaying the local message history.

Source code in pydantic_ai/realtime/elevenlabs.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    ws: ClientConnection,
    *,
    dial: Callable[[], Awaitable[ClientConnection]] | None = None,
    reconnect: ReconnectPolicy | None = None,
    input_transcription_enabled: bool = True,
    interrupts_response_on_speech: bool = False,
    model_name: str | None = None,
    model_name_getter: Callable[[], str | None] | None = None,
    observes_output_audio: bool = True,
    audio_output_sample_rate: int = DEFAULT_AUDIO_SAMPLE_RATE,
    prune_tool_items: bool = False,
    keep_tool_items: AbstractSet[str] = frozenset(),
    manual_turns: bool = False,
    strip_audio_tags: bool = True,
) -> None:
    # ElevenLabs transcribes every spoken turn, so its transcripts arrive (and belong in history) even when
    # `input_transcription_model=None` asked for none.
    del input_transcription_enabled
    super().__init__(
        ws,
        dial=dial,
        reconnect=reconnect,
        interrupts_response_on_speech=interrupts_response_on_speech,
        model_name=model_name,
        model_name_getter=model_name_getter,
        observes_output_audio=observes_output_audio,
        audio_output_sample_rate=audio_output_sample_rate,
        prune_tool_items=prune_tool_items,
        keep_tool_items=keep_tool_items,
        manual_turns=manual_turns,
    )
    # Semantic VAD commits the speech it hears on its own, unless turn detection is off.
    self._lifecycle: _ElevenLabsLifecycle = _ElevenLabsLifecycle(server_vad=not manual_turns)
    # See `ElevenLabsRealtimeModelSettings.elevenlabs_strip_audio_tags`.
    self._strip_audio_tags = strip_audio_tags
    # The streamed transcript of each output item under way, with its audio tags removed, and the tags each
    # response's transcripts held (see `_strip_transcript_tags`).
    self._tag_strippers: dict[str | None, AudioTagStripper] = {}
    self._audio_tags: dict[str | None, list[str]] = {}
    # When this connection last sent the server anything, on the event loop's clock (see `_keep_alive`).
    self._last_sent = 0.0
    # Tool calls ElevenLabs gave up on when it started a reply to the user before their results were in (see
    # `_abandon_outstanding_tool_calls`).
    self._abandoned_tool_calls: set[str] = set()
    # Responses with tool calls that a user message joined the conversation after: the next response to start can
    # be the reply to it, which abandons their calls (see `_abandon_outstanding_tool_calls`).
    self._interjected: set[str] = set()

ElevenLabs realtime API model, for the Eleven Realtime speech-to-speech models.

Pass provider='elevenlabs' (the default, which reads ELEVENLABS_API_KEY) or an ElevenLabsProvider constructed with api_key= or a data-residency base_url=. The session is configured and driven through the OpenAI Realtime protocol over a WebSocket; WebRTC is not supported.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION model

TYPE: ElevenLabsRealtimeModelName

provider

The provider to use for authentication and the base URL. Defaults to 'elevenlabs'.

TYPE: Provider[AsyncHTTPClient] | str DEFAULT: 'elevenlabs'

settings

Model settings used as defaults for realtime sessions. With a reconnect policy, a dropped connection is re-dialed and the local message history replayed into it.

TYPE: RealtimeModelSettings | None DEFAULT: None

Optional override for the realtime model profile, merged over the provider's — a partial dict, or a callable taking the resolved profile and returning the one to use.

TYPE: RealtimeModelProfileSpec | None DEFAULT: None

Source code in pydantic_ai/realtime/elevenlabs.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    model: ElevenLabsRealtimeModelName,
    *,
    provider: Provider[AsyncHTTPClient] | str = 'elevenlabs',
    settings: RealtimeModelSettings | None = None,
    profile: RealtimeModelProfileSpec | None = None,
) -> None:
    if isinstance(provider, str):
        provider = infer_provider(provider)
    if not isinstance(provider, ElevenLabsProvider):
        # Reading `api_key` off a foreign provider would fail with an `AttributeError` instead of the real mistake.
        raise UserError(
            "`ElevenLabsRealtimeModel` requires an `ElevenLabsProvider` or `provider='elevenlabs'`; "
            f'got {provider.name!r}.'
        )
    self._elevenlabs_provider = provider
    super().__init__(model, provider=_ElevenLabsOpenAIProvider(provider), settings=settings, profile=profile)

🌐 এই পেজের সহজ বাংলা সংস্করণ এখনো তৈরি হচ্ছে

আপাতত নিচে মূল ইংরেজি লেখাটি দেখানো হচ্ছে। এই অংশের অন্য পেজগুলোতে সহজ বাংলা ব্যাখ্যা পাবেন।

অফিসিয়াল ইংরেজি পেজ

The ElevenLabs Agents realtime provider. Requires the elevenlabs-agents-realtime optional group (pip install "pydantic-ai-slim[elevenlabs-agents-realtime]").

items.title: pydantic_ai.realtime.elevenlabs_agents
items.text:
ElevenLabs Agents provider for realtime voice sessions.

ElevenLabs Agents runs a cascaded pipeline (realtime ASR + a configurable LLM + ElevenLabs TTS + a server-side turn-taking model) behind a pre-provisioned agent, reached over the agent WebSocket (wss://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/conversation?agent_id=...). So unlike the other realtime providers, the model here wraps a hosted agent addressed by its agent_id, and Pydantic AI takes ownership of as much of the conversation as ElevenLabs allows per-conversation:

  • Instructions, LLM choice, first message, language, voice, TTS knobs, and text-only mode are pushed through conversation_initiation_client_data.conversation_config_override. Every overridable field is gated by a per-field toggle under Security > Overrides in the agent's settings (platform_settings.overrides); the connect-time preflight fetches the agent and raises a UserError naming the exact toggle when an override the session needs is not permitted. (The raw elevenlabs_agents_config_override escape hatch skips this check by design and is judged by the server after the handshake instead.) When the Pydantic AI agent defines no instructions, the ElevenLabs-side prompt is inherited silently.
  • Tool declarations cannot be sent inline per-conversation: client tools are workspace entities referenced from the agent. By default the preflight errors on mismatch between the session's ToolDefinitions and the agent's client tools; the opt-in elevenlabs_agents_tool_sync='sync' setting instead creates/updates the workspace tools and re-points the agent's tool_ids over REST before dialing.
  • Turn-taking, VAD, ASR configuration, audio formats, and platform settings (auth, privacy, guardrails, knowledge bases) stay owned by the ElevenLabs agent configuration.

Requires the websockets package, available via the elevenlabs-agents-realtime optional group (REST preflight uses Pydantic AI's own HTTP client, so no ElevenLabs SDK is needed):

pip install "pydantic-ai-slim[elevenlabs-agents-realtime]"

items.title: ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModelSettings
items.text:
Bases: RealtimeModelSettings

Settings specific to ElevenLabs Agents realtime sessions.

Every elevenlabs_agents_* field below that maps to a conversation_config_override entry requires the matching override toggle to be enabled under Security > Overrides in the agent's settings; the connect-time preflight raises UserError naming the toggle otherwise.

Of the shared settings, output_modality='text' maps to the conversation.text_only override, and a tool_choice of 'none' or an allow-list to the agent.prompt.tool_ids override, which narrows the agent's attached tools for the conversation (a choice that forces a tool call raises). max_tokens, parallel_tool_calls, async_tool_calls, and thinking have no per-conversation surface on the agent WebSocket and are silently ignored, per the shared settings contract. turn_detection cannot be configured (ElevenLabs' server-side turn model is always on), input_transcription_model=None cannot be honored (ASR cannot be disabled per-conversation), and reconnect is unsupported (ElevenLabs' experimental, text-only resume isn't used), so each of those raises rather than silently under-delivering.

items.title: elevenlabs_agents_tool_sync instance-attribute
items.text:
elevenlabs_agents_tool_sync

How to reconcile the session's tools with the agent's client tools at connect time.

  • 'error' (default): raise UserError describing every difference between the session's ToolDefinitions and the agent's client tools, so the two can never silently disagree.
  • 'sync': make the workspace match Pydantic AI over REST before dialing: create missing client tools, update differing ones, and re-point the agent's tool_ids (dropping client tools the session doesn't define; ElevenLabs-side webhook/MCP/system tools are left untouched). This mutates workspace state shared by every conversation with the agent, which is why it is opt-in.
  • 'off': skip the check and trust the agent's own tool definitions, e.g. for client tools configured on the ElevenLabs side with settings Pydantic AI doesn't sync. A call to a tool the session does not define reaches the tool manager like any other call and is answered with the standard unknown-tool error, which lands in the session's history.

items.title: elevenlabs_agents_strip_audio_tags instance-attribute
items.text:
elevenlabs_agents_strip_audio_tags

Whether to remove expressive audio tags such as [laughs] from the agent's transcripts. Defaults to True.

With an expressive TTS model such as eleven_v3_conversational, the agent's LLM writes tags into its reply to direct the delivery, and they are part of the transcript ElevenLabs sends, though they aren't spoken. They are removed from the transcript, streamed and in history alike, and the tags a response's transcript held are kept, in order and without brackets, in its provider_details['audio_tags']. Only lowercase words in square brackets count as tags, so citations ([1]), Markdown links, and placeholders like [Your Name] are kept. Set this to False to keep the transcript exactly as ElevenLabs sends it, tags included.

items.text:
elevenlabs_agents_config_override

Raw values deep-merged last into conversation_config_override, the escape hatch mirroring google_config_overrides. Not preflight-checked against the override toggles; the server still rejects non-permitted fields.

def __init__(
    self,
    agent_id: str,
    *,
    provider: Provider[AsyncHTTPClient] | str = 'elevenlabs',
    settings: RealtimeModelSettings | None = None,
    profile: RealtimeModelProfileSpec | None = None,
) -> None:
    super().__init__(settings=settings, profile=profile)
    self.agent_id = agent_id
    self._warned_context_usage = False
    from ..providers.elevenlabs import ElevenLabsProvider

    if isinstance(provider, str):
        provider = infer_provider(provider)
    if not isinstance(provider, ElevenLabsProvider):
        # The REST preflight and signed-URL auth below read the ElevenLabs-specific `api_key` off
        # the provider; a foreign one would fail with an `AttributeError` instead of the real mistake.
        raise UserError(
            f"`ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModel` requires an `ElevenLabsProvider` or `provider='elevenlabs'`; "
            f'got {provider.name!r}.'
        )
    self._provider = provider

items.title: ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeConnection
items.text:
ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeConnection(
    ws,
    *,
    conversation_id=None,
    text_output=False,
    strip_audio_tags=True
)

Bases: RealtimeConnection

A live WebSocket connection to an ElevenLabs Agents conversation.

Source code in pydantic_ai/realtime/elevenlabs_agents.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    ws: ClientConnection,
    *,
    conversation_id: str | None = None,
    text_output: bool = False,
    strip_audio_tags: bool = True,
) -> None:
    self._ws = ws
    self._conversation_id = conversation_id
    self._context_limit_tokens: int | None = None
    self._text_output = text_output
    # The streamed text of the response under way, with its audio tags removed (see `_AudioTagStripper`).
    self._tag_stripper = _AudioTagStripper() if strip_audio_tags else None
    # Calls the agent fired without expecting a result (`expects_response=false`): the session
    # still settles them locally, but their `ToolResult` must never go back on the wire.
    self._fire_and_forget_tool_call_ids: set[str] = set()
    # Whether the model has streamed response output since the last turn boundary, so a boundary
    # event never finalizes a turn that produced nothing.
    self._response_open = False
    # The agent message the open response streams, once its text parts have named it, and the turn it is in.
    self._open_response_id: str | None = None
    self._open_event_id: int | None = None
    # What ElevenLabs said the user heard of the agent messages, by `agent_response_correction`, for the frame
    # under way to record on them, whether their responses are under way or over.
    self._cuts: list[OutputItemCut] = []
    self._turn_interrupted = False
    self._tail: _AudioTail | None = None
    # The MCP calls ElevenLabs runs itself, reported as native tool parts: those whose call part is out, and
    # those denied whose outcome ElevenLabs hasn't reported, which the response they belong to records.
    self._mcp_calls: set[str] = set()
    self._warned_mcp_approval = False
    self._calls_open = False
    """Whether the response under way made tool calls, and ends once no more come."""
    self._mcp_denied: dict[str, NativeToolReturnPart] = {}
    self._native_part_index = 0
    # Whether the conversation is waiting in the workspace's concurrency queue, where the server
    # plays hold audio over regular `audio` frames: that audio is no response of the agent's.
    self._queued = False
    # The responses, spoken turns, and inputs are worked out from the order of what is sent and
    # received. The protocol does carry ids (`event_id` per turn, `response_id` on the whole-text
    # `agent_response`, `in_response_to_ids`), but each arrives only with a response's *end*, while
    # a response has to be announced with its first audio, and a tool round shares one `event_id`
    # between the response that calls the tool and the one that answers its result. So the ids only
    # correct what the order said: `in_response_to_ids` names the text inputs a reply answers.
    # The user's words are transcribed (and sent) before the agent's LLM answers them, never after.
    self._lifecycle = _CascadeLifecycle()
    # A barge-in on the response under way, which only its (truncated) terminal is yet to follow.
    self._deferred_cut: RealtimeResponseInterruptedEvent | None = None
    # Whether the lifecycle saw that barge-in before the cut-off response's terminal came.
    self._cut_shown = False

model_name

The LLM behind the agent only surfaces in the context_usage report, which an agent sends only with it in its client_events, so it would name the model of some responses and not others, and the session falls back to ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModel.model_name.

context_limit_tokens

The context window of the LLM behind the agent, as last reported by a context_usage event.

None until the agent reports one, which requires context_usage in its conversation.client_events list. It is a property of the conversation, not of a response, so it is kept here rather than summed into the session's usage, and the session's context_window_used is only known once such a report arrives.

items.title: send async
items.text:
send(content)

Send content to the ElevenLabs Agents conversation.

Accepts BinaryAudio (raw PCM16 mono at the agent's input rate), a str text turn, TextContext (a contextual_update: context the agent reads from its next turn on, without interrupting or answering), and ToolResult. Manual turn-taking verbs, response cancellation, truncation, and images are not supported by the conversation WebSocket.

Source code in pydantic_ai/realtime/elevenlabs_agents.py 
async def send(self, content: RealtimeInput) -> Sequence[LifecycleEvent]:
    """Send content to the ElevenLabs Agents conversation.

    Accepts `BinaryAudio` (raw PCM16 mono at the agent's input rate), a `str` text turn,
    `TextContext` (a `contextual_update`: context the agent reads from its next turn on, without
    interrupting or answering), and `ToolResult`. Manual turn-taking verbs, response
    cancellation, truncation, and images are not supported by the conversation WebSocket.
    """
    with self._lifecycle.sending(content) as input_id:
        sent = await self._send(content, input_id)
    if not sent:
        # A fire-and-forget call's result: the agent asked for none, so none will be answered.
        self._lifecycle.input_unanswerable(input_id)
    # ElevenLabs acknowledges nothing: where the input joined the conversation is known now.
    return self._lifecycle.take_pending()

items.text:
🌐 এই পেজের সহজ বাংলা সংস্করণ এখনো তৈরি হচ্ছে

আপাতত নিচে মূল ইংরেজি লেখাটি দেখানো হচ্ছে। এই অংশের অন্য পেজগুলোতে সহজ বাংলা ব্যাখ্যা পাবেন।

অফিসিয়াল ইংরেজি পেজ

The Gemini Live API provider. Requires the google-realtime optional group (pip install "pydantic-ai-slim[google-realtime]").

GoogleRealtimeModel runs over the google-genai SDK (which manages the WebSocket transport). Gemini expects 16 kHz PCM input (output is 24 kHz), produces one response modality per session, and natively accepts live video frames sent as BinaryImage. It exposes Gemini Live's session and generation configuration through GoogleRealtimeModelSettings — shared turn-taking via TurnDetection, with finer Gemini-specific control via AutomaticVAD in google_vad plus google_activity_handling/google_turn_coverage, voice via google_voice, and long-session ContextCompression — with resilience via session resumption + a ReconnectPolicy in the reconnect setting.

items.title: pydantic_ai.realtime.google
items.text:
Gemini Live API provider for realtime speech-to-speech (and live video) sessions.

Built on the google-genai SDK, which manages the WebSocket transport for you. Available via the google optional group:

pip install "pydantic-ai-slim[google-realtime]"

Unlike the OpenAI provider, Gemini wants 16 kHz PCM input audio (output is 24 kHz), produces a single response modality per session (audio or text), and natively accepts a stream of video frames sent as BinaryImage.

Use provider='google' for the Gemini Developer API, or provider='google-cloud' / GoogleCloudProvider for Google Cloud with Application Default Credentials.

A Live session speaks in one voice. google-genai refuses a multi-speaker voice config on the Live path, Gemini 2.5 native-audio models reject it, and the Gemini 3.1 Flash Live and 3.8 Live models accept it but ignore the per-speaker voices.

items.title: google_affective_dialog instance-attribute
items.text:
google_affective_dialog

Whether to enable emotion-aware delivery.

Not supported by the Gemini 3.1 Flash Live and 3.8 Live models, so connect raises UserError if it's enabled for one of them (see google_supports_affective_dialog).

items.title: google_proactive_audio instance-attribute
items.text:
google_proactive_audio

Whether the model may decide when to respond, including staying silent on input not addressed to it. Useful for "react to the camera" experiences.

Always on for the Gemini 3.8 Live models, so there it can be left unset. They reject an explicit False, which is never sent: False just leaves the field out.

Gemini serves proactivity on the Developer API's v1alpha only. A provider built from an API key opens the session's Live connection with a separate v1alpha client, leaving its own client as it is. A client the caller built has to be on v1alpha already: connect raises UserError naming the fix otherwise. Unavailable on Vertex AI, whose version line has no v1alpha.

items.title: google_input_transcription instance-attribute
items.text:
google_input_transcription

Whether to transcribe input audio. Defaults to True.

When False, user turns are recorded as retained audio when available, or as content-less placeholders otherwise. Takes precedence over the shared input_transcription_model, whose None also turns transcription off here.

items.title: google_output_transcription instance-attribute
items.text:
google_output_transcription

Whether to transcribe output audio. Defaults to True.

When False, retain output audio if assistant audio turns need to appear in history. Assistant audio without a transcript cannot be handed off or seeded.

items.text:
google_vad

Gemini-specific server-side voice activity detection settings.

When present, this fully overrides the cross-provider turn_detection setting. google_vad={'disabled': True} raises a UserError, like turn_detection=False: Pydantic AI does not expose Gemini activity markers or manual turn controls, so the resulting session could not drive turns.

Which realtime input is attached to a turn — 'activity_only', 'all_input' (everything between turns too), or 'all_video' (all video frames plus audio during activity; ideal for live-camera use). Absent uses the provider default.

items.title: google_enable_session_resumption instance-attribute
items.text:
google_enable_session_resumption

Whether to request session-resumption handles, which let a re-dial restore the server-side conversation.

When absent, handles are requested exactly when a reconnect policy is set. An explicit False cannot be combined with a reconnect policy: a re-dial without resumption would lose the conversation, so connect raises UserError rather than silently reconnecting into a model that remembers nothing.

items.title: google_async_tool_calls instance-attribute
items.text:
google_async_tool_calls

Deprecated: use the shared async_tool_calls setting instead.

Translated (with a deprecation warning) when a session connects; an async_tool_calls in the same settings wins.

items.title: GoogleRealtimeModelProfile
items.text:
Bases: RealtimeModelProfile

Profile for Gemini Live models, adding the Gemini-specific fields to the shared realtime profile.

Mirrors the GoogleModelProfile / ModelProfile split on the request-response side.

items.title: google_thinking_levels instance-attribute
items.text:
google_thinking_levels

Thinking levels the Live model accepts. Default: unset.

Same meaning as google_thinking_levels on a standard model: unset means the full GOOGLE_THINKING_LEVELS scale, and a unified thinking effort snaps to the nearest level in the set.

items.title: google_thinking_always_enabled instance-attribute
items.text:
google_thinking_always_enabled

Whether the model always reasons, so its API requires a thinking level. Default: False.

Mirrors ModelProfile.thinking_always_enabled. A session that sets no thinking still sends the cheapest level the model accepts, and thinking=False means "as little as possible" rather than a thinking_budget=0 the model would reject. gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking closes the handshake with 1007 Thinking level must be specified for this model without a level.

items.title: google_async_tool_calls_by_default instance-attribute
items.text:
google_async_tool_calls_by_default

Whether the model runs a tool call asynchronously when its declaration sets no behavior. Default: False.

True of the Gemini 3.8 Live family, where Google made NON_BLOCKING the default. Tool calls stay blocking unless async_tool_calls asks otherwise, so on such a model the declaration says BLOCKING explicitly instead of leaving it unset.

items.title: google_requires_async_tool_calls instance-attribute
items.text:
google_requires_async_tool_calls

Deprecated: use async_tool_call_mode='always' instead.

Translated (with a deprecation warning) when the profile is resolved: True becomes async_tool_call_mode='always', and False, which left the choice to the other flags, is dropped.

items.title: google_closes_tool_call_turn_separately instance-attribute
items.text:
google_closes_tool_call_turn_separately

Whether the model closes a tool-call turn with a turn_complete of its own. Default: False.

Vertex's half-cascade gemini-live-2.5-flash sends one when the tool-call generation ends (usage only, no output), whether or not the results have arrived yet, and another after speaking the answer (verified live); other Live models send only the answer's. With this set, the first of the two is reported as the tool-call response's usage rather than a turn boundary, so the exchange isn't reported complete before the answer is spoken. Set by default on Vertex AI only, where it was verified.

items.title: google_input_cuts_off_reply instance-attribute
items.text:
google_input_cuts_off_reply

Whether text or a tool result that reaches the model mid-generation cuts the reply off. Default: False.

The model then reports the reply interrupted and complete (cancelling the tool calls it was waiting on, on gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview) and answers the input in the next turn, so the cut-off reply answers only the request that started it. Verified live for gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview and gemini-3.8-live, which also report the user's speech (voice_activity) when that is what cut the reply off. Vertex's gemini-live-2.5-flash cuts a reply off too, but doesn't say whether speech did it, so it is left off; the native-audio models finish the reply instead, and answer the input after it.

items.title: google_supports_async_tool_call_scheduling instance-attribute
items.text:
google_supports_async_tool_call_scheduling

Whether the model takes a scheduling field on an async tool call's result. Default: False.

Separate from whether the call runs asynchronously at all: that is decided when the call is declared, while scheduling says how its result enters the speech the model is producing when it arrives. Pydantic AI sends FunctionResponseScheduling.INTERRUPT, so the result cuts in rather than waiting for the model to go idle. gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking runs every call asynchronously but paces results against its own reasoning, and closes the session with 1007 Function response scheduling is not supported for this model if the field is sent at all.

items.title: google_supports_affective_dialog instance-attribute
items.text:
google_supports_affective_dialog

Whether the model takes google_affective_dialog. Default: True.

When False, connect raises UserError for a session that enables it, rather than opening one the provider rejects. False for the gemini-3.1-flash-live and gemini-3.8-live families, which don't support affective dialog: gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview refuses the handshake with 1007 Request contains an invalid argument, and the 3.8 models open the session and then close it with the same error on the first send.

items.title: google_supported_mime_types_in_tool_returns instance-attribute
items.text:
google_supported_mime_types_in_tool_returns

Media types a tool result can carry inside its function response. Default: ().

The realtime counterpart of google_supported_mime_types_in_tool_returns on a standard model: content of these types attached to a tool return (a BinaryContent or a downloaded ImageUrl) goes in FunctionResponse.parts, and any other media raises UserError with the result unsent. PNG, JPEG, WebP, and plain text on the Gemini 3.x Live models, which read them; gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-* doesn't, and the 3.x models close the session on a PDF.

items.title: google_supports_seeding_function_parts instance-attribute
items.text:
google_supports_seeding_function_parts

Whether seeded tool calls and results go in as native function parts. Default: False.

When True, prior ToolCallParts and ToolReturnParts are seeded as function_call and function_response parts, sent as the session's initial history (history_config), rather than projected as readable text. True of the Gemini 3.8 Live models. gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-* rejects function parts in seeded turns, and gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview loses history seeded that way when a reconnect resumes the session.

items.title: google_text_turns_see_video_frames instance-attribute
items.text:
google_text_turns_see_video_frames

Whether a typed turn sees an image sent just before it as a live video frame. Default: True.

session.send(image) sends the image as a video frame, which a spoken turn sees. On a model where a typed turn doesn't, the most recent image sent in the last 10 seconds is sent again in the typed turn's own content, ahead of the text. Every Gemini Live model probed misses it: gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview, gemini-3.8-live and its extended-thinking variant answer that they can't see an image, and gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-* and Vertex's gemini-live-2.5-flash misread it.

items.title: GoogleRealtimeModel dataclass
items.text:
GoogleRealtimeModel(
    model, *, provider="google", settings=None, profile=None
)

Bases: RealtimeModel

Gemini Live API model.

Session and generation configuration is read from GoogleRealtimeModelSettings, passed through settings as model-level defaults or as model_settings when opening a session.

Authentication and the underlying google-genai client come from a Provider, mirroring GoogleModel. Pass provider='google' (the default) for the Gemini Developer API (reads GOOGLE_API_KEY / GEMINI_API_KEY), provider='google-cloud' for Vertex AI (Application Default Credentials, useful where org policy disallows API keys), or a GoogleProvider / GoogleCloudProvider instance for a custom key, client, or region. Gemini Live is available on both surfaces.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION model

The model name, e.g. gemini-3.8-live (low-latency voice), gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking (reasons in the background while it speaks, and always runs tools asynchronously), or gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-latest (an alias that tracks the newest native-audio Live model).

TYPE: GoogleRealtimeModelName

provider

The provider to use for authentication and API access — 'google' (Gemini Developer API, the default) or 'google-cloud' (Vertex AI), or a Provider instance.

TYPE: Literal['google', 'google-cloud', 'gateway'] | Provider[Client] DEFAULT: 'google'

settings

Model-level defaults for session and generation configuration.

TYPE: RealtimeModelSettings | None DEFAULT: None

profile

Optional override for the realtime model profile, merged over the provider's — a partial dict, or a callable taking the resolved profile and returning the one to use. Mirrors profile= on a standard Model, and is the escape hatch when a model name doesn't identify the model (e.g. an Azure deployment named something other than its model).

TYPE: RealtimeModelProfileSpec | None DEFAULT: None

Source code in pydantic_ai/realtime/google.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    model: GoogleRealtimeModelName,
    *,
    provider: Literal['google', 'google-cloud', 'gateway'] | Provider[Client] = 'google',
    settings: RealtimeModelSettings | None = None,
    profile: RealtimeModelProfileSpec | None = None,
) -> None:
    if settings:
        # Translated here so the deprecation warning points at the caller's line.
        settings = _translate_legacy_settings(cast(GoogleRealtimeModelSettings, settings), stacklevel=3)
    super().__init__(settings=settings, profile=profile)
    self.model = model
    if isinstance(provider, str):
        provider_name = 'gateway/google-cloud' if provider == 'gateway' else provider
        provider = cast('Provider[Client]', infer_provider(provider_name))
    self._provider = provider

items.title: GoogleRealtimeConnection
items.text:
GoogleRealtimeConnection(
    session,
    *,
    profile=None,
    provider_name="google",
    dial=None,
    reconnect=None,
    input_transcription_enabled=True,
    async_tool_calls=False,
    provider_url="",
    text_output=False
)

Bases: RealtimeConnection

A live connection to the Gemini Live API, backed by a google-genai session.

Source code in pydantic_ai/realtime/google.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    session: AsyncSession,
    *,
    profile: RealtimeModelProfile | None = None,
    provider_name: str = 'google',
    dial: Callable[[str | None], Awaitable[AsyncSession]] | None = None,
    reconnect: ReconnectPolicy | None = None,
    input_transcription_enabled: bool = True,
    async_tool_calls: bool = False,
    provider_url: str = '',
    text_output: bool = False,
) -> None:
    self._session = session
    # Whether the session asked for text rather than audio (`output_modality='text'`). A text-only model
    # streams its text answer as `output_transcription` (`gemini-robotics-er-2-streaming-preview`, verified
    # live), which is then the answer itself, written rather than spoken.
    self._text_output = text_output
    self._profile = profile if profile is not None else DEFAULT_REALTIME_PROFILE
    self._input_transcription_enabled = input_transcription_enabled
    self._reconnects_used = 0
    self._gave_up = False
    self._async_tool_calls_enabled = async_tool_calls
    # Whether the model takes a `scheduling` field at all: extended thinking paces results against its
    # own reasoning and closes the session if one is sent. A connection built without a profile keeps
    # sending it, as it did before the flag existed; `GoogleRealtimeModel.connect` always passes one.
    self._async_tool_call_scheduling_enabled = profile is None or cast('GoogleRealtimeModelProfile', profile).get(
        'google_supports_async_tool_call_scheduling', False
    )
    self._closes_tool_call_turn_separately = profile is not None and cast(
        'GoogleRealtimeModelProfile', profile
    ).get('google_closes_tool_call_turn_separately', False)
    # Provider name stamped onto native-tool history parts (grounding / code execution), matching the
    # classic `GoogleModel` (`NativeToolCallPart.provider_name`), so a turn's history is provider-tagged
    # identically whether it came from a realtime session or a classic run.
    self._provider_name = provider_name
    # The provider's HTTP base URL, which is how genai-prices identifies a provider for pricing.
    self._provider_url = provider_url
    # internal call id -> (tool name, Gemini call id), so a `ToolResult` can echo the name and id
    # Gemini requires. Calls Gemini sends without an id get a synthetic one so parallel id-less
    # calls don't collide.
    self._tool_calls: dict[str, tuple[str, str | None]] = {}
    # (tool name, Gemini call id) of calls a resumed session lost but still waits on, and whether they
    # have been answered on the current session; see `_answer_lost_tool_calls`.
    self._unanswered_lost_tool_calls: list[tuple[str, str | None]] = []
    self._lost_tool_calls_answered = False
    # The typed turns a resumed session may not have, oldest first: each stays until a handle arrives
    # after the exchange that answered it ended. A handle's arrival time says nothing about which inputs it
    # covers, but a server that withholds handles mid-turn only issues one once a turn is over.
    self._uncovered_typed_turns: list[_TypedTurn] = []
    # How much audio has gone out on this connection, in seconds: where Gemini's `voice_activity` offsets point.
    self._audio_seconds = 0.0
    # Where in that audio each recent input other than audio went out, oldest first (see `_voice_activity`).
    self._sent_at: deque[tuple[float, InputId]] = deque(maxlen=64)
    # Whether the server withholds handles while it works on a turn, seen as an update without a
    # handle while a typed turn is outstanding. Gemini 2.5 takes up every typed turn that way, and a
    # session resumed from the handle before it doesn't have the turn. 3.8 never does, and (verified
    # live) resumes with the turn known. Learned once rather than from the latest update, which a
    # drop right after a send can beat.
    self._withholds_handles_mid_turn = False
    # Orders the answers for lost calls, which both the receive loop and `send()` may send, so an
    # input waiting on them never overtakes them.
    self._send_lock = Lock()
    self._native_part_index = 0
    # The `tool_call_id` generated for the most recent `executable_code` part, reused to pair the
    # following `code_execution_result` return with its call — mirroring the classic `GoogleModel`
    # streaming path, which threads a single id from the code part to its result.
    self._code_execution_tool_call_id: str | None = None
    # `dial` re-establishes a configured session from the latest resumption handle; with a
    # `reconnect` policy it recovers a dropped connection.
    self._dial = dial
    self._reconnect = reconnect
    self._resumption_handle: str | None = None
    self._turn_interrupted = False
    # Whether the model has streamed response output (audio, transcript, text, or native-tool
    # parts) since the last `turn_complete`. A dropped-and-redialed connection never continues an
    # in-flight turn (session resumption restores conversation state, not the generation;
    # verified live), so when this is set at reconnect time the turn's boundary would otherwise
    # never arrive — see `frames`, which closes the orphaned turn before the reconnect event.
    self._turn_open = False
    # On a model whose typed turns don't see video frames, the most recent image sent and when (by
    # `time.monotonic()`), for the next typed turn to carry again. See `send`.
    self._text_turns_see_video_frames = cast('GoogleRealtimeModelProfile', self._profile).get(
        'google_text_turns_see_video_frames', True
    )
    self._tool_return_mime_types = cast('GoogleRealtimeModelProfile', self._profile).get(
        'google_supported_mime_types_in_tool_returns', ()
    )
    self._recent_image: tuple[BinaryImage, float] | None = None
    # Whether the turn's latest output is a tool-call frame, with nothing said since. A model that
    # `google_closes_tool_call_turn_separately` closes that turn with its own `turn_complete` when the
    # tool-call generation ends, before speaking the answer; see `_map_message`. It's taken for that
    # only once every result is sent (with results still pending, the session holds the reply open
    # anyway), and only the first time: the next boundary always ends the turn, so an empty answer
    # completes.
    self._tool_call_turn_unanswered = False
    # Which response, user turn, and input each message is about (see `frames()`).
    cuts_off = cast('GoogleRealtimeModelProfile', self._profile).get('google_input_cuts_off_reply', False)
    self._lifecycle = (_CutOffLifecycle if cuts_off else InferredLifecycle)(transcribes=input_transcription_enabled)

items.text:
send(content)

Send content to the Gemini Live API.

Accepts BinaryAudio (raw PCM16, 16kHz, mono), a str text turn, TextContext (text sent with turn_complete=False, so it waits for the next turn), BinaryImage (a live video frame), and ToolResult. The manual turn-taking verbs are not supported (Gemini uses automatic VAD).

Source code in pydantic_ai/realtime/google.py 
async def send(self, content: RealtimeInput) -> Sequence[LifecycleEvent]:
    """Send content to the Gemini Live API.

    Accepts `BinaryAudio` (raw PCM16, 16kHz, mono), a `str` text turn, `TextContext` (text sent
    with `turn_complete=False`, so it waits for the next turn), `BinaryImage` (a live video
    frame), and `ToolResult`. The manual turn-taking verbs are not supported (Gemini uses
    automatic VAD).
    """
    turn: _TypedTurn | None = None
    with self._lifecycle.sending(content) as input_index:
        while self._unanswered_lost_tool_calls and not self._lost_tool_calls_answered:
            # Whatever reaches a resumed session first is consumed by an exchange stuck on calls it lost,
            # so those are answered ahead of any input (see `_answer_lost_tool_calls`). The lock orders
            # this with the receive loop's own answer, so the input can't overtake it; the loop answers
            # again if a re-dial replaced the session while an answer was on the wire.
            async with self._send_lock:
                await self._answer_lost_tool_calls()
        # Tracked from before the send, so a handle or answer arriving while it is on the wire counts.
        # Only needed to tell a reconnect what it lost, so not tracked without a reconnect policy.
        turn = _TypedTurn(input_index) if isinstance(content, str) and self._reconnect is not None else None
        if turn is not None:
            self._uncovered_typed_turns.append(turn)
        try:
            await self._send(content)
        except BaseException:
            # A reconnect noticed meanwhile has already let go of the list it was in.
            if turn is not None and turn in self._uncovered_typed_turns:
                self._uncovered_typed_turns.remove(turn)
            raise
        if isinstance(content, BinaryAudio):
            self._audio_seconds += len(content.data) / (2 * INPUT_SAMPLE_RATE)
        else:
            self._sent_at.append((self._audio_seconds, input_index))
    if turn is not None:
        turn.sending = False
    # Gemini acknowledges nothing: where the input joined the conversation is known now, if it is.
    return self._lifecycle.take_pending()

items.title: pydantic_ai.realtime.lifecycle
items.text:
The lifecycle events a realtime connection yields, for implementing a realtime provider.

The codec vocabulary says what the model said, but not which response it belongs to, when that response began or ended, or which of the session's inputs it answers. Only the connection sees the provider frames that settle those questions, so a RealtimeConnection states them outright, interleaved with its codec events in the RealtimeFrames it yields from frames():

  • a response is bracketed by exactly one ResponseStarted and one ResponseEnded, and its content arrives only in between;
  • ResponseStarted.answers names the inputs whose reply the response is, which is what wait_for_reply() waits for, and AnswersRevised corrects them as the connection learns better: claimed while the response is under way, released until its reply (tool rounds included) is over;
  • a spoken user turn starts with UserTurnStarted, joins the conversation with UserTurnEnded, and gets no more audio or transcript after UserTurnClosed (which drops one that hadn't joined);
  • InputAdded marks where an input joined the provider's conversation, so history can follow the provider's order;
  • InputLost and ResponseRequestRefused settle the inputs no response will ever answer, and ToolCallsAbandoned the tool calls whose results none will;
  • OutputItemDetails keeps what the provider says about an output item on the part it makes, and OutputItemCut records that the listener heard only part of it, even after its response ended.

An input is identified by its position among every send() call made on the connection, counting from 0, as InputRejected.input_index identifies it.

A protocol that identifies its responses, turns, and inputs (as the OpenAI Realtime API does) is best translated directly. One that identifies none of them, like Gemini Live and OpenAI GPT-Live, can have InferredLifecycle work them out from the order of what the connection sends and receives.

items.title: InferredLifecycle
items.text:
InferredLifecycle(*, transcribes=True)

Works out a connection's lifecycle events from the order of what it sends and receives.

For a protocol that identifies no responses, spoken turns, or inputs, as Gemini Live and OpenAI GPT-Live don't. The connection, in its send, sends each input inside sending (which reports it, and reports it failed if sending it raises) and returns what the send settled (take_pending). It passes the codec events each provider message makes through frame_for to get the frame to yield, and reports a dropped connection (connection_lost). A connection whose codec events are an async iterable of their own can have frames do the last two.

What it works out:

  • A response starts with its first output (audio, a transcript, a native tool part, a tool call), and ends at its ResponseDone; a response that makes tool calls ends with them, or, when they are reported with response_usage_follows, at the usage report that follows them. Its id is made up, so it is recorded as no provider's (ResponseStarted.provider_id=False).
  • A response whose calls are reported with response_continues goes on past them, as the model keeps talking, until its ResponseDone, until the result of one of them goes out (a result directly follows the response that made its call), or until a spoken turn joins the conversation, which follows it too. What the model says after that, before the ResponseDone that ends its turn, is a response of its own. If the model was mid-sentence when the result went out, that is the rest of the sentence, which answers nothing; otherwise it answers the result. Cut off while one of those calls still runs, the response ends completed: its tool round goes on.
  • A response answers every input that asked for one (a str turn, a tool result, a CreateResponse) and wasn't answered when it started (ResponseStarted.basis='inferred').
  • A spoken turn starts with its first input transcript, joins the conversation as the reply to it starts, and has its whole transcript once that reply ends, unless the transcript is marked final before. A turn the provider identifies (its transcripts carry an item_id) is named by that id, and waits for its final transcript. Without input transcription, audio sent since the last reply is a turn of its own, with no transcript, when the model next replies to speech.
  • An input joins the conversation when it is sent, unless a reply is under way or owed: it then reached the provider while the model was working on that reply, and follows it.
  • A dropped connection loses the response under way and every reply still owed.

These are the defaults; a provider that departs from them gets a subclass overriding these extension points:

  • transcripts_lag_replies (True): whether the provider transcribes the user's words after the model started answering them.
  • audio_starts_response (True): whether output audio is the model speaking, so a response starts with it.
  • untranscribed_audio_is_a_turn (True): whether audio the model replies to before any transcript of it came is a spoken turn of its own.
  • inputs_cut_off_replies (False): whether an input that reaches the provider mid-generation cuts the reply off, leaving it to the next.
  • takes_turn(codec) (False): whether a provider message has the model take the turn, whatever its output shows.
PARAMETER DESCRIPTION transcribes

Whether the session has the user's speech transcribed: if not, audio alone makes a spoken turn. A setting of the session's (input transcription), not of the provider.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

Source code in pydantic_ai/realtime/_inferred_lifecycle.py 
def __init__(self, *, transcribes: bool = True) -> None:
    """Track a connection's lifecycle.

    Args:
        transcribes: Whether the session has the user's speech transcribed: if not, audio alone makes a spoken
            turn. A setting of the session's (input transcription), not of the provider.
    """
    self._transcribes = transcribes
    self._inputs = 0
    self._pending: list[LifecycleEvent] = []
    """Events that come outside any message (an input sent), yielded ahead of the next one."""
    self._responses = 0
    self._open: str | None = None
    """The response under way."""
    self._open_named = False
    """Whether the provider named the response under way, by the `response_id` of its content."""
    self._open_answers: tuple[InputId, ...] = ()
    """The inputs the response under way answers, oldest first."""
    self._open_said = False
    """Whether the response under way said (or called) anything yet."""
    self._open_calls: list[str] = []
    """The tool calls the response under way made."""
    self._continued_calls: list[str] = []
    """The tool calls the response under way went on past (`ToolCall.response_continues`) that are still running,
    with no result out: it goes on until its terminal, or until one of their results goes out."""
    self._said_since_call = False
    """Whether the response under way said anything since its latest tool call."""
    self._split_turn = False
    """A response ended as the result of one of the calls it went on past went out, with the provider's turn still
    open: that turn's terminal ends only what started since."""
    self._tail = False
    """The model was mid-sentence when that result went out: the next output is the rest of it, a response that
    answers nothing."""
    self._calling: dict[str, tuple[str, tuple[InputId, ...]]] = {}
    """The response that ended at each tool call (until the next response starts), and the inputs it answers: its
    reply goes on in the answer to the calls."""
    self._spoken_since = -1
    """The last input sent when the provider heard the user start speaking: only an input sent after it can have
    cut a reply off (see `inputs_cut_off_replies`). (Sending audio says nothing: a microphone streams silence too.)"""
    self._ended_by_usage: str | None = None
    """The response a usage report or its tool call just ended: its terminal, if one follows, ends nothing more."""
    self._cut_off = False
    """Whether the response under way was cut off (`RealtimeResponseInterruptedEvent`): more output is another."""
    self._deferred: ResponseDone | None = None
    """The terminal of a response the model said the exchange continues past (`interaction_status=IN_PROGRESS`):
    it stays open for the tool call it was stalling for, and ends at anything else."""
    self._calls_awaiting_usage = False
    """The open response made tool calls whose (empty) usage report closes it."""
    self._unanswered: list[InputId] = []
    """Inputs that asked for a reply no response has started yet, oldest first."""
    self._held: list[InputId] = []
    """Inputs sent while a reply was under way or owed, which join the conversation after that reply."""
    self._turns = 0
    self._turn: _Turn | None = None
    self._turn_reply: tuple[str, str] | None = None
    """The response replying to the joined turn, whose end closes the turn's transcript."""
    self._unprompted_reply: str | None = None
    """The response under way, if the model started it on its own with no transcript of speech to reply to yet."""
    self._audio_since_reply = False
    """Audio went out since the last reply started: without transcription, the next turn of speech."""
    self._continues: str | None = None
    """A response the model ended saying the exchange goes on, which the next response carries on from."""
    self._unnamed_committed = False
    """A turn joined the conversation, unnamed and without words yet (see `_commit_unnamed`)."""
    self._speaking = False
    """The provider heard the user start speaking, in a turn it didn't name, and not stop yet."""
    self._transcribed_while_speaking = False
    """Words came since the user started speaking: the speech is the turn they transcribe."""
    self._spoken_unanswered: str | None = None
    """A spoken turn that joined the conversation ahead of a reply that hasn't started yet."""
    self._uncommit: _Uncommit | None = None
    """How to take back the latest commit, while its send may still fail."""
    self._identified: set[str] = set()
    """The turns the provider named, by item id."""
    self._replayed_items: set[str] = set()
    self._replayed_calls: set[str] = set()
    """The items and tool calls a resumed conversation replays (`ConversationItemCreated.replayed`)."""

items.title: transcripts_lag_replies class-attribute
items.text:
transcripts_lag_replies = True

Whether the provider can transcribe the user's words after the model started answering them, as most do.

A transcript that starts while a reply nobody asked for is under way is then the speech that reply answers, rather than speech over it. A subclass for a provider that transcribes as the user speaks (and so reports speech over a reply while the reply is still going) sets it to False.

items.title: audio_starts_response class-attribute
items.text:
audio_starts_response = True

Whether output audio is the model speaking, so a response starts with it.

A subclass for a provider whose output is a continuous track, silent between replies, sets it to False, and says where the model takes the turn with takes_turn instead.

items.title: inputs_cut_off_replies class-attribute
items.text:
inputs_cut_off_replies = False

Whether an input that reaches the provider while it generates a reply cuts that reply off.

The next reply then answers the input, so a reply cut off (ResponseStarted through a cancelled ResponseEnded) answers only the oldest input it was taken to answer, as that one started it, or none if it said nothing; and a reply whose tool calls the provider cancels answers only the oldest too. That is, unless the provider heard the user start speaking after those inputs went out (speech_heard()): then the user may have cut the reply off, as ever. The rest are released (AnswersRevised.released) to the next reply. A subclass for a provider that cuts its reply off this way (Gemini Live's 3.x models do) sets it to True.

items.title: untranscribed_audio_is_a_turn class-attribute
items.text:
untranscribed_audio_is_a_turn = True

Whether audio the model replies to before any transcript of it came is a spoken turn of its own.

A subclass for a provider that replies to speech only once it has transcribed it (a cascaded pipeline, say) sets it to False, so audio no transcript names, like a microphone streaming before a greeting, makes no turn. Without input transcription (transcribes=False), audio is the only sign of speech, and always makes a turn.

items.title: input_sent
items.text:
input_sent(content)

An input is about to go out: note whether it asks for a reply, and where it joins the conversation.

Call it for every send(), before anything in it can fail, as the session numbers its inputs that way. Returns the input's id, for input_failed and input_unanswerable.

Source code in pydantic_ai/realtime/_inferred_lifecycle.py 
def input_sent(self, content: RealtimeInput) -> InputId:
    """An input is about to go out: note whether it asks for a reply, and where it joins the conversation.

    Call it for every `send()`, before anything in it can fail, as the session numbers its inputs that way.
    Returns the input's id, for `input_failed` and `input_unanswerable`.
    """
    input_id = self._inputs
    self._inputs += 1
    if isinstance(content, BinaryContent) and content.is_audio:
        self._audio_since_reply = True
        return input_id
    if isinstance(content, CommitAudio):
        # The audio sent since the last turn is one now: it joins the conversation as the commit arrives. (Undone
        # if the commit never goes out.)
        turn = self._turn
        self._uncommit = _Uncommit(
            input_id=input_id,
            pending=len(self._pending),
            audio_since_reply=self._audio_since_reply,
            unnamed_committed=self._unnamed_committed,
            spoken_unanswered=self._spoken_unanswered,
            joined=turn if turn is not None and not turn.joined else None,
        )
        self._commit_turn()
        return input_id
    if isinstance(content, ToolResult) and content.tool_call_id in self._continued_calls:
        # A result directly follows the response that made its call: what the model says from here is after it.
        self._split(self._pending)
    if isinstance(content, (str, CreateResponse)):
        # What the model says next may be the reply to this, rather than the rest of a sentence a result cut into.
        self._tail = False
    if isinstance(content, CreateResponse):
        # A request for a reply, with nothing of its own to join the conversation.
        self._unanswered.append(input_id)
        return input_id
    self._announce_committed(self._pending)
    if self._reply_owed():
        # It reaches the provider while the model works on a reply, which it follows. (A response that answers
        # it places it ahead of itself, should that come first.)
        self._held.append(input_id)
    else:
        # Nothing is going on: it joins the conversation as it arrives.
        self._pending.append(InputAdded(input_id=input_id))
    if isinstance(content, (str, ToolResult)):
        self._unanswered.append(input_id)
    return input_id

items.title: input_failed
items.text:
input_failed(input_id)

The input never went out (its send raised): forget it.

Source code in pydantic_ai/realtime/_inferred_lifecycle.py 
def input_failed(self, input_id: InputId) -> None:
    """The input never went out (its send raised): forget it."""
    if (uncommit := self._uncommit) is not None and uncommit.input_id == input_id:
        # A commit that never went out committed nothing.
        self._uncommit = None
        del self._pending[uncommit.pending :]
        self._audio_since_reply = uncommit.audio_since_reply
        self._unnamed_committed = uncommit.unnamed_committed
        self._spoken_unanswered = uncommit.spoken_unanswered
        if uncommit.joined is not None:
            uncommit.joined.joined = False
    self._unanswered = [unanswered for unanswered in self._unanswered if unanswered != input_id]
    self._held = [held for held in self._held if held != input_id]
    self._pending = [event for event in self._pending if event != InputAdded(input_id=input_id)]

input_unanswerable(input_id)

An input went (or was meant to go) out, but the provider will never reply to it.

Source code in pydantic_ai/realtime/_inferred_lifecycle.py 
def input_unanswerable(self, input_id: InputId) -> None:
    """An input went (or was meant to go) out, but the provider will never reply to it."""
    if input_id in self._unanswered:
        self._unanswered.remove(input_id)
        # (Held behind the reply under way, it doesn't join the conversation after it either.)
        self._held = [held for held in self._held if held != input_id]
        self._pending.append(InputLost(input_ids=(input_id,)))

items.title: sending
items.text:
sending(content)

Report an input a connection's send() is sending, around the sending itself: yields the input's id.

It is input_sent going in, and input_failed if the block raises. The connection then returns take_pending() (see the example in Implementing a connection).

Source code in pydantic_ai/realtime/_inferred_lifecycle.py 
@contextmanager
def sending(self, content: RealtimeInput) -> Generator[InputId]:
    """Report an input a connection's `send()` is sending, around the sending itself: yields the input's id.

    It is [`input_sent`][pydantic_ai.realtime.lifecycle.InferredLifecycle.input_sent] going in, and
    [`input_failed`][pydantic_ai.realtime.lifecycle.InferredLifecycle.input_failed] if the block raises. The
    connection then returns [`take_pending()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.lifecycle.InferredLifecycle.take_pending]
    (see the example in [Implementing a connection](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/main/docs/realtime.md)).
    """
    input_id = self.input_sent(content)
    try:
        yield input_id
    except BaseException:
        self.input_failed(input_id)
        raise

items.title: take_pending
items.text:
take_pending()

The events the inputs sent since the last frame settled.

Where each joined the conversation, or that it will go unanswered. A connection returns them from send(), so the session applies them before anything it reads next, and puts them at the head of a frame of its own (like the one it reports a reconnect in). frame_for() takes any still waiting into the frame it makes.

Source code in pydantic_ai/realtime/_inferred_lifecycle.py 
def take_pending(self) -> list[LifecycleEvent]:
    """The events the inputs sent since the last frame settled.

    Where each joined the conversation, or that it will go unanswered. A connection returns them from
    [`send()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.codec.RealtimeConnection.send], so the session applies them before anything it
    reads next, and puts them at the head of a frame of its own (like the one it reports a reconnect in).
    [`frame_for()`][pydantic_ai.realtime.lifecycle.InferredLifecycle.frame_for] takes any still waiting into the
    frame it makes.
    """
    pending, self._pending = self._pending, []
    # (A commit whose events are out can't be taken back any more.)
    self._uncommit = None
    return pending

items.title: speech_heard
items.text:
speech_heard(*, after=None)

The provider heard the user start speaking, which may cut a reply off (see inputs_cut_off_replies).

A RealtimeInputSpeechStartEvent says so; a connection whose provider reports speech some other way (Gemini Live's voice_activity) calls this, or every reply cut off is taken for one an input cut off. after is the id of the last input sent before the user started speaking, when the provider says where in the audio that was: -1 if they started before any input, and by default every input sent so far, as the report may come late.

Source code in pydantic_ai/realtime/_inferred_lifecycle.py 
def speech_heard(self, *, after: InputId | None = None) -> None:
    """The provider heard the user start speaking, which may cut a reply off (see `inputs_cut_off_replies`).

    A `RealtimeInputSpeechStartEvent` says so; a connection whose provider reports speech some other way (Gemini
    Live's `voice_activity`) calls this, or every reply cut off is taken for one an input cut off. `after` is the id
    of the last input sent before the user started speaking, when the provider says where in the audio that was:
    `-1` if they started before any input, and by default every input sent so far, as the report may come late.
    """
    self._spoken_since = max(self._spoken_since, self._inputs - 1 if after is None else after)

items.title: frame_for
items.text:
frame_for(codec)

The frame to yield for the codec events one provider message makes, with the lifecycle events around them.

Source code in pydantic_ai/realtime/_inferred_lifecycle.py 
def frame_for(self, codec: Sequence[RealtimeCodecEvent]) -> RealtimeFrame:
    """The frame to yield for the codec events one provider message makes, with the lifecycle events around them."""
    turn_taken = self.takes_turn(codec)
    frame: RealtimeFrame = [*self.take_pending()]
    if any(isinstance(event, RealtimeResponseInterruptedEvent) for event in codec):
        # The user cut in, and the message reports what they said ahead of the cut: that is new speech, not
        # more of the turn being answered, whose transcript is over.
        closed: list[LifecycleEvent] = []
        self._unprompted_reply = None
        self._close_turn(closed)
        frame.extend(closed)
    for event in codec:
        before, after = self._event(event, takes_turn=turn_taken)
        frame.extend(before)
        frame.append(event)
        frame.extend(after)
    if turn_taken:
        started: list[LifecycleEvent] = []
        self._ensure_response(started)
        frame.extend(started)
    return frame

items.title: frames async
items.text:
frames(events)

Frames for a connection's codec events, one event to a frame, ending with what the end of events loses.

For a connection whose codec events are an async iterable of their own, and end with the connection.

Source code in pydantic_ai/realtime/_inferred_lifecycle.py 
async def frames(self, events: AsyncIterable[RealtimeCodecEvent]) -> AsyncIterator[RealtimeFrame]:
    """Frames for a connection's codec events, one event to a frame, ending with what the end of `events` loses.

    For a connection whose codec events are an async iterable of their own, and end with the connection.
    """
    iterator = aiter(events)
    try:
        async for event in iterator:
            yield self.frame_for([event])
        lost: RealtimeFrame = [*self.connection_lost()]
        yield lost
    finally:
        if isinstance(iterator, AsyncGenerator):
            await iterator.aclose()

items.title: connection_lost
items.text:
connection_lost()

The connection dropped (and is being re-dialed, or is gone): nothing under way on it will finish.

A re-dial never resumes a generation, even when it resumes the session, so the response under way is lost, and so is every reply still owed. A spoken turn the model was about to answer is in the conversation all the same, with what transcript it has.

Source code in pydantic_ai/realtime/_inferred_lifecycle.py 
def connection_lost(self) -> list[LifecycleEvent]:
    """The connection dropped (and is being re-dialed, or is gone): nothing under way on it will finish.

    A re-dial never resumes a generation, even when it resumes the session, so the response under way is
    lost, and so is every reply still owed. A spoken turn the model was about to answer is in the
    conversation all the same, with what transcript it has.
    """
    events = self.take_pending()
    self._announce_committed(events)
    self._deferred = self._continues = None
    self._split_turn = self._tail = False
    if self._open is not None:
        self._end(events, status='lost')
    if lost := tuple(self._unanswered):
        self._unanswered.clear()
        events.append(InputLost(input_ids=lost))
    # Ending the response closed the turn it replied to: one still here is the next, not joined yet.
    if (turn := self._turn) is not None:
        self._turn = None
        if not turn.joined:
            events.append(UserTurnEnded(turn_id=turn.id))
        # (Its transcript was still to come, or it would be over: what it has is all there will be.)
        events.append(UserTurnClosed(turn_id=turn.id))
    self._place_held(events)
    if self._transcribes:
        # What audio was sent is the turn its transcript names, or nothing. (Without transcripts, it is still
        # what the user said, for a commit or the next reply to make a turn of.)
        self._audio_since_reply = False
    return events

items.title: AnswersRevised dataclass
items.text:
AnswersRevised(*, response_id, claimed=(), released=())

Bases: LifecycleEvent

Which inputs a response answers turned out different from what its ResponseStarted said.

A connection that works its responses' answers out (basis='inferred') can learn better as the response goes on: GPT-Live answers text sent mid-reply in the speech already under way, and Gemini cuts off a reply that an input reaches mid-generation, leaving that input to the next one. claimed is valid while the response is under way, released until its reply (tool rounds included) is over.

It moves no message: history keeps every input where it joined the conversation.

claimed = ()

Inputs still owed a reply that this response answers after all. Only while it is under way (before its ResponseEnded).

Inputs this response was said to answer that it doesn't: a later response answers them, naming them in its ResponseStarted.answers (or in a claimed of its own).

Before its ResponseEnded, or after it while its reply goes on: in the answer to its tool calls, say, which the provider can cancel when an input cuts the turn off.

Bases: LifecycleEvent

The provider says the listener heard only part of one spoken output item, before or after its response ended.

Generation outruns playback, so the reply the user cuts off has usually ended already. Its message in history is marked interrupted, and swapped for a copy in the same position, as one the session cuts off itself on a barge-in is: a snapshot of history already handed out doesn't change. Like ElevenLabs' agent_response_correction.

items.title: StaleEvent dataclass
items.text:
StaleEvent(event)

A codec event about a response that has already ended: a repeated terminal, or content trailing it.

The application still receives event, as it always has, but nothing applies it to the conversation: the response it is about is over. A connection that can't tell such events apart (most can't) never yields one.

items.title: ToolCallsAbandoned dataclass
items.text:
ToolCallsAbandoned(*, tool_call_ids)

Bases: LifecycleEvent

The provider gave up on these tool calls: no response will answer their results.

Eleven Realtime gives up on a finished response's calls once it starts a reply to the user before their results are in, and GPT-Live on the calls its delegated backend asked for when that backend fails. The calls still run, and each result is recorded in history (and still sent, where the provider takes it), but nothing waits for a reply to it: the exchange is over once nothing else is owed. Unlike a ToolCallCancelled, it doesn't stop them.

🌐 এই পেজের সহজ বাংলা সংস্করণ এখনো তৈরি হচ্ছে

আপাতত নিচে মূল ইংরেজি লেখাটি দেখানো হচ্ছে। এই অংশের অন্য পেজগুলোতে সহজ বাংলা ব্যাখ্যা পাবেন।

অফিসিয়াল ইংরেজি পেজ

The OpenAI Realtime API provider. Requires the realtime and openai optional groups (pip install "pydantic-ai-slim[realtime,openai]").

OpenAIRealtimeModelSettings configures the session, including shared turn-taking via TurnDetection (or False for push-to-talk). For finer control, openai_turn_detection accepts ServerVAD or SemanticVAD and fully overrides the shared setting. Resilience comes from the reconnect setting: a ReconnectPolicy in RealtimeModelSettings.

items.title: pydantic_ai.realtime.openai
items.text:
OpenAI Realtime API provider for speech-to-speech sessions.

Connects to wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime over a WebSocket and maps the OpenAI event protocol to the shared realtime event types.

Requires the websockets and openai packages, available via the realtime and openai optional groups:

pip install "pydantic-ai-slim[openai-realtime]"

The server detects when the user starts and stops speaking and (by default) commits the audio and triggers a response automatically. Unset fields fall back to the provider defaults.

Whether to automatically generate a response when the user stops speaking. Defaults to True.

If set, auto-trigger a response after this much idle time with no detected speech. Defaults to the provider default.
