items.title: Approval Reviewer
items.text:
Let a second model approve the low-risk tool calls that need approval, and leave the rest to a person.

Source

While Pydantic AI Harness is on 0.x releases, the API may change between minor releases; when it does, deprecation warnings and release-note migration guidance tell you (or your agent) exactly how to upgrade. See the version policy.

Approval Reviewer or Tool Call Judge?

Both ask a second model one yes/no question about a tool call, but give it opposite powers. Use Tool Call Judge when you want a model to say no: its yes blocks a call, whether or not a person is watching. Use Approval Reviewer when you want a model to say yes on a person's behalf: it reviews only calls that already need approval, its no approves the call, and everything else still goes to the person. A judge cannot do the second job, because it runs when a call executes, after the person has already approved it.

items.title: The problem
items.text: Human approval is the dependable gate for a tool like run_shell, but most of the calls it stops are harmless: ls, git status, rg TODO. A person asked to approve every one of them stops reading the requests, and the request that mattered gets the same click as the rest. Allowlists cut the volume, but which calls are risky depends on the arguments, and a list only covers the shapes you anticipated.

items.title: The solution
items.text:
ApprovalReviewer answers approval requests before a person sees them. You give it one risk question; for each call that needs approval, a second model answers yes, no, or unsure. A no approves the call on the person's behalf and it runs in the same run step. Everything else is left for the person, exactly as it would have been without the reviewer.

The reviewer can only take a question off the person's plate. It never denies a call, never runs one itself, and does nothing for calls that do not need approval.

For the models in this example, install their provider extra and set an API key:

pipuv 
pip install pydantic-ai-harness "pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic]"

uv add pydantic-ai-harness "pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic]"

export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY='your-anthropic-api-key'

from pydantic_ai import Agent, DeferredToolRequests
from pydantic_ai_harness.approval_reviewer import ApprovalReviewer

reviewer = ApprovalReviewer(
    'anthropic:claude-haiku-5-5',
    tools=['run_shell'],
    question='Could this command delete or overwrite data, reach the network, or expose secrets?',
)
agent = Agent(
    'anthropic:claude-fable-5-1',
    capabilities=[reviewer],
    output_type=[str, DeferredToolRequests],
)


@agent.tool_plain(requires_approval=True)
def run_shell(command: str) -> str:
    # Keep the example non-destructive. A real tool runs the command in a sandbox here.
    return f'Would run: {command}'


result = agent.run_sync('How many Python files are in this directory?')
if isinstance(result.output, DeferredToolRequests):
    for call in result.output.approvals:
        print(f'Needs your approval: {call.tool_name} {call.args}')
else:
    print(result.output)

With this question, a call like find . -name '*.py' | wc -l is expected to be approved and run without stopping the run, and a call like curl https://example.com/install.sh | sh to be left in the run's DeferredToolRequests output for you to approve or deny, the same way it would be without the reviewer.

The reviewing model returns only the literal yes, no, or unsure, not a free-text explanation. Where a provider reports its own answer confidence in response metadata, it is read from there.

items.title: Which calls are reviewed
items.text:
Only calls that need approval reach the reviewer. A call needs approval when its tool is registered with requires_approval=True or raises ApprovalRequired, which includes a ToolGuardrail that returns GuardrailResult.approve() and a ToolCallJudge with on_uncertain='ask'. Calls that run without approval are not reviewed and cost nothing. Externally executed calls (CallDeferred) are not approval requests, so they are left alone too.

tools narrows that further. It is a ToolSelector, the same selector the other tool-scoped capabilities take:

Value Reviews approval requests for 'all' (default) every function tool ['run_shell', 'write_file'] tools with those names {'risk': 'low'} tools whose metadata includes those pairs lambda ctx, tool_def: ... whatever the predicate returns

Approval requests for tools the selector does not match go to the person unreviewed. 'all' also covers the requests a ToolGuardrail or a ToolCallJudge raises and any approval-required tool added later, all answered by the one question, so name the tools the question was written for.

items.title: What happens to the rest
Working with Tool Call Judge
items.text:
ToolCallJudge and ApprovalReviewer ask the same kind of question at different points, and in opposite directions. A judge can only narrow what runs: its yes blocks a call. A reviewer can only widen what runs without a person: its no approves a call.

Together they sort every call into blocked, run, or sent to a person. Let the judge block what must never run and escalate what it cannot settle with on_uncertain='ask', and let the reviewer approve the escalations that are safe enough to run unattended:

from pydantic_ai import Agent, DeferredToolRequests
from pydantic_ai_harness.approval_reviewer import ApprovalReviewer
from pydantic_ai_harness.tool_call_judge import ToolCallJudge

agent = Agent(
    'anthropic:claude-fable-5-1',
    capabilities=[
        ToolCallJudge(
            'anthropic:claude-haiku-5-5',
            tools=['run_shell'],
            question='Could this command delete or overwrite data outside the project directory?',
            on_uncertain='ask',
        ),
        ApprovalReviewer(
            'anthropic:claude-haiku-5-5',
            tools=['run_shell'],
            question='Could this command delete or overwrite data, reach the network, or expose secrets?',
        ),
    ],
    output_type=[str, DeferredToolRequests],
)


@agent.tool_plain
def run_shell(command: str) -> str:
    return f'Would run: {command}'
Judge Reviewer What happens no not asked the call runs yes not asked the call is blocked unsure or failed no the call is approved, and the judge is asked again before it runs unsure or failed yes, unsure, or failed the call is left for the person

run_shell is not registered with requires_approval=True, so the judge's escalations are the only approval requests the reviewer sees for it. On a tool that also requires approval, the reviewer answers those requests too, under the same question.

A call the reviewer approves is judged again, like any approved call (working with human approval): a yes still blocks it, and an unsure now lets it run. An escalated call that runs costs two judgements and one review.

Scope the reviewer's tools away from the judge's when you want the judge's escalations to reach a person.

items.title: What the reviewer sees
items.text:
By default, one review is a fresh internal-agent run whose entire input is:

  • the fixed reviewer instructions, including your question
  • a <tool_call> block with the tool name and the call's arguments as JSON, as the model made them: the same call a person would be shown

The outer agent's conversation, instructions, and tool results are not forwarded. That keeps each review small and cheap, and it keeps the reviewer away from text the agent read from pages, files, and other tool results.

Set include_conversation=True when the question needs the conversation that led to the call, such as "does this go beyond what the user asked for?". The reviewer then also receives a <conversation> block: user messages, assistant messages, tool calls, and tool results, clamped to the most recent conversation_window tokens (estimated at ~4 characters per token). System prompts and thinking parts are left out.

Turning it on widens the reviewer's own prompt-injection surface, because the transcript includes third-party content, and a reviewer that is talked into answering no approves the call. The instructions label both blocks as untrusted data, and the < of every opening or closing framework tag inside either block is escaped (<tool_call>, <conversation>, and Pydantic AI framing tags such as <system>), so content cannot end its block or forge another. Everything else is embedded as written. That reduces the risk rather than removing it.

Either way, what the reviewer is shown leaves the process: a call's arguments go to the reviewing model's provider, including for calls the reviewer then leaves for the person. Where a tool's arguments can carry credentials or customer data, scope tools away from it, or route the reviewer to a provider you already trust with that data.

items.title: Risk tiers
items.text:
Like ToolCallJudge, ApprovalReviewer asks one question and takes one answer rather than grading risk on a scale against a threshold: a model's self-reported severity is not calibrated across models, prompts, or days, so a threshold on it would not mean what it says.

Tiering is expressed with the tools selector instead. Calls to a tool the reviewer selects can be approved by the model; calls to a tool it does not select always go to a person. Mark tools by what a wrong approval would cost, and select only the tiers you are willing to hand to a model:

from pydantic_ai import Agent, DeferredToolRequests
from pydantic_ai_harness.approval_reviewer import ApprovalReviewer

agent = Agent(
    'anthropic:claude-fable-5-1',
    output_type=[str, DeferredToolRequests],
    capabilities=[
        ApprovalReviewer(
            'anthropic:claude-haiku-5-5',
            tools={'risk': 'low'},
            question='Could this command delete or overwrite data, reach the network, or expose secrets?',
        ),
    ],
)


@agent.tool_plain(requires_approval=True, metadata={'risk': 'low'})
def run_shell(command: str) -> str:
    return f'Would run: {command}'


@agent.tool_plain(requires_approval=True, metadata={'risk': 'high'})
def deploy(environment: str) -> str:
    return f'Would deploy to {environment}'

A run_shell call the reviewer answers no for runs without asking anyone; every deploy call goes to a person, because no reviewer selects it.

For a different question per tool, add more than one reviewer, each with its own selector, question, and model. Every reviewer receives the requests the ones before it left, so a call is approved when any reviewer that selects it answers no. Give reviewers non-overlapping selectors, so that each tool's calls are cleared by the question written for it.

items.title: Using a decision model
items.text:
Whether a call is risky is a classification, which is what a decision model such as TypeSafe's Jev answers, cheaper and faster than a language model. Pass one as the reviewer's model and nothing else changes: the review is one pick-one question over yes, no, and unsure, worded by your question and the reviewer instructions, about the <tool_call> block. The decision model's confidence in its answer is recorded on ApprovalReview.confidence and the approval_reviewer.confidence span attribute.

For the models in the example below, install their provider extras and set API keys:

pipuv 
pip install pydantic-ai-harness "pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic,typesafe]"

uv add pydantic-ai-harness "pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic,typesafe]"

export TYPESAFE_API_KEY='your-typesafe-api-key'
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY='your-anthropic-api-key'

A no approves the call however unsure the model was of it. To have a language model decide the reviews the decision model was unsure of, put the decision model in front of one in a FallbackModel that falls back on low confidence:

from pydantic_ai import ModelAPIError, ModelResponse
from pydantic_ai.models.fallback import FallbackModel
from pydantic_ai_harness.approval_reviewer import ApprovalReviewer


def unsure(response: ModelResponse) -> bool:
    confidence = (response.provider_details or {}).get('confidence', {})
    return any(value < 0.8 for value in confidence.values())


reviewer = ApprovalReviewer(
    FallbackModel('typesafe:jev-latest', 'anthropic:claude-haiku-5-5', fallback_on=[ModelAPIError, unsure]),
    tools=['run_shell'],
    question='Could this command delete or overwrite data, reach the network, or expose secrets?',
)

The handler runs on every model in the chain, and a language model reports no confidence, so the fallback model's answer stands. Tune the bar on labelled calls of your own, as in tuning a threshold on your own data, and once you have, pin the Jev version you tuned it against (typesafe:jev-1.13.0) rather than jev-latest. Jev treats the text it judges as data rather than as hostile, so arguments written to steer its answer can move it (what Jev answers badly): keep the safety boundary in place, as with any reviewer.

items.title: Composition
items.text:
Calls in one batch are reviewed one at a time, in the order the model made them, so a batch of approval requests adds one review per selected call to the run step's latency.

Each review's model usage is added to the outer run's usage and respects its usage limits. A review claims its request on the shared usage before it calls the model, so the run's request_limit bounds the reviews too. A review the budget cannot fit is not made, and the call is left for the person.

items.title: Durable execution
items.text:
Inside a durable workflow or flow (Temporal, DBOS, Prefect) each review is a durable operation. It is checkpointed under the name <agent>__capability__<id>.review, so a replay reuses the recorded answer instead of asking the model again: a call approved on the first execution is approved on every replay, and the reviewer is billed once.

on_review is not part of the durable operation, so a replay calls it again with the recorded review. Deduplicate on ApprovalReview.tool_call_id when the callback writes to an external system.

A durable operation is addressed by the capability's id, and ApprovalReviewer has no default one, because several reviewers on one agent is a normal shape. So a reviewer on a durable-capable agent needs an explicit id, distinct per reviewer:

from pydantic_ai_harness.approval_reviewer import ApprovalReviewer

reviewer = ApprovalReviewer(
    'anthropic:claude-haiku-5-5',
    id='shell-reviewer',
    tools=['run_shell'],
    question='Could this command delete or overwrite data, reach the network, or expose secrets?',
)

Without one, Pydantic AI refuses to bind the agent, naming the fix. Outside durable execution id stays optional.

items.title: Observability
items.text:
Every review opens a review tool approval span on the run's tracer:

Attribute Value approval_reviewer.tool tool name approval_reviewer.tool_call_id call identifier approval_reviewer.model_result yes, no, unsure, or error approval_reviewer.decision approve or ask approval_reviewer.confidence answer confidence from provider metadata, when reported approval_reviewer.error.type exception type when the review failed approval_reviewer.arguments the call's arguments, only when trace_include_content is on

The internal reviewer agent is not instrumented, so its prompt (which contains the call's arguments) is not recorded even when global instrumentation is on. Its usage is still added to the outer run's usage. Core reports the approvals themselves in the run's DeferredToolResultsEvent.

Pass on_review to observe the same decisions from application code:

from pydantic_ai_harness.approval_reviewer import ApprovalReview, ApprovalReviewer

reviews: list[ApprovalReview] = []
reviewer = ApprovalReviewer(
    'anthropic:claude-haiku-5-5',
    tools=['run_shell'],
    question='Could this destroy data or leak secrets?',
    on_review=reviews.append,
)

An exception raised by on_review is not caught: it ends the run, and approvals already made in the same batch are not applied.

items.title: Safety boundary
items.text: An approval a model gives is a model's decision, on input the agent partly controls. ApprovalReviewer is a filter that decides which requests a person no longer sees, not a security boundary. Keep authentication, authorization, argument validation, least privilege, sandboxing, and recovery controls inside or below any tool that destroys data, spends money, exposes secrets, or cannot be undone, and scope tools to the calls where an automatic approval is acceptable.

items.title: Agent specs
items.text: ApprovalReviewer publishes an agent-spec schema for a string model identifier, the question, the serializable tools forms ('all', a name list, a metadata match), include_conversation, conversation_window, and the standard capability fields. A live Model, a predicate selector, and the on_review callback are code-only.

items.title: Ask User
items.text:
Let the model ask the user multiple-choice questions mid-run and wait for the answers.

Source

While Pydantic AI Harness is on 0.x releases, the API may change between minor releases; when it does, deprecation warnings and release-note migration guidance tell you (or your agent) exactly how to upgrade. See the version policy.

items.title: The problem
items.text: An agent given an ambiguous task either guesses or buries a question in its output and stops. Guessing wastes a run; a question in prose is only found by a person reading the whole answer. The model needs a way to ask a small, structured question and get the answer back as data.

items.title: The solution
items.text:
AskUser exposes one tool, ask_user_question. The model passes one to ten questions, each with a short header, the question text, two to six options (a label and an optional description), and multi_select when several answers are allowed. The capability validates the call, hands it to your answerer, and returns the picked labels keyed by header. If the user declines, the model is told so and the run continues.

The capability owns the schema and validation. It never prints, reads stdin, or imports a terminal library: the answerer is whatever puts the questions in front of a person, and you supply it. There is no default, because a capability that reads stdin is unusable from a server.

from pydantic_ai import Agent
from pydantic_ai_harness import AskUser
from pydantic_ai_harness.ask_user import AskUserAnswer, AskUserRequest, AskUserResponse


async def pick_first(request: AskUserRequest) -> AskUserResponse:
    answers = [AskUserAnswer(header=q.header, selected=(q.options[0].label,)) for q in request.questions]
    return AskUserResponse(answers=tuple(answers))


agent = Agent('anthropic:claude-fable-5-1', capabilities=[AskUser(answerer=pick_first)])

pick_first stands in for a real UI. CLAI ships a terminal menu built on the same protocol; a web form would be another.

items.title: Writing an answerer
items.text:
An Answerer is one async callable: it takes an AskUserRequest and returns an AskUserResponse. A plain async def qualifies; a class with async def __call__ does too.

  • AskUserRequest.questions holds the validated Question objects; AskUserRequest.id distinguishes concurrent or repeated calls so a UI can match its reply to the request.
  • A completed AskUserResponse carries one AskUserAnswer per question, keyed by header, with the picked option labels in selected: exactly one unless the question is multi_select, at least one either way, and no label twice.
  • An answerer may instead return AskUserAnswer(header=q.header, custom_answer='My own answer'). Leave selected empty. Custom text must be nonblank and contain no control characters other than newlines and no format characters such as zero-width spaces, joiners and bidirectional overrides, so run check_response on text a user typed. Its length is not limited, so cap free text that arrives from a client before returning it. The model receives it as a one-item list under the question's header. Whether to offer text entry is up to the answerer; the model cannot request it.
  • When the user declines, return AskUserResponse(cancelled=True) with no answers. The tool result tells the model the user declined; nothing is raised into the run.
  • A response that does not fit the request (an unknown header, a label the question did not offer, several labels on a single-select question, a missing answer) is a bug in the answerer and raises ValueError, which fails the run. check_response is exported so an answerer can validate before returning.
  • By default, two ask_user_question calls in one model response reach the answerer concurrently, so serialize in the answerer if your UI shows one request at a time. Other tool calls from that response may run while the user decides: an answer shapes the model's next response, not calls it already made. To run a response's calls one at a time, wrap the run in with Agent.parallel_tool_call_execution_mode('sequential'):.
  • The model writes the questions, and a prompt injection can make it ask for a password or a token. Present the questions as coming from the model, not as a system or sign-in prompt.

items.title: Bounding the wait
items.text:
The run waits inside the tool call for the answerer to return. Set timeout, in seconds, to bound that wait. When it runs out, the answerer is cancelled, AskUserAnsweredEvent fires with timed_out=True and a cancelled response, and the model is told the user did not answer in time (the TIMED_OUT result) and continues.

The timeout cancels the answerer, so the answerer must be cancellable. A thread cannot be cancelled: run blocking work with anyio.to_thread.run_sync(..., abandon_on_cancel=True), or the run waits for the thread and then uses its late answer. An abandoned thread keeps running, so a terminal answerer should read input with an async prompt library rather than input() in a thread, which would take the next line the user types.

AskUser(answerer=pick_first, timeout=300)

items.title: Pausing the run until the user answers
items.text:
A web server or a durable worker often cannot hold a run open while a person decides. Pass answerer=None and every ask_user_question call is deferred instead: the run ends with DeferredToolRequests output, so your output_type must include it, and you answer in a later run, from the same process or another one.

  • AskUserRequest.from_tool_call(call) rebuilds the validated request from a pending call. Its id is the call's tool_call_id, the same request AskUserRequestedEvent carried before the run paused.
  • ask_user_result(request, response) checks the response like an answerer's (raising ValueError if it does not fit) and renders the tool result the model would have got inline. Pass it in DeferredToolResults.calls under the call's ID.
  • No AskUserAnsweredEvent fires for a deferred call: the answer comes from you, in the next run.
from pydantic_ai import Agent, AgentRunResult, DeferredToolRequests, DeferredToolResults, ModelMessage
from pydantic_ai_harness import AskUser
from pydantic_ai_harness.ask_user import TOOL_NAME, AskUserRequest, AskUserResponse, ask_user_result

agent = Agent(
    'anthropic:claude-fable-5-1',
    output_type=[str, DeferredToolRequests],
    capabilities=[AskUser(answerer=None)],
)


def pending_questions(requests: DeferredToolRequests) -> dict[str, AskUserRequest]:
    """What the paused run is waiting on, keyed by tool call ID: show these to the user."""
    return {
        call.tool_call_id: AskUserRequest.from_tool_call(call)
        for call in requests.calls
        if call.tool_name == TOOL_NAME
    }


async def resume(
    messages: list[ModelMessage],
    questions: dict[str, AskUserRequest],
    responses: dict[str, AskUserResponse],
) -> AgentRunResult[str | DeferredToolRequests]:
    """Answer the paused run's questions and carry on."""
    calls = {call_id: ask_user_result(request, responses[call_id]) for call_id, request in questions.items()}
    return await agent.run(message_history=messages, deferred_tool_results=DeferredToolResults(calls=calls))

Keep the paused run's all_messages() and its pending questions wherever you keep sessions, then call resume when the answers arrive. timeout needs an answerer to bound, so combining it with answerer=None raises UserError.

items.title: Watching without answering
items.text:
Two CapabilityEvents let anything else in the run observe the exchange:

Event When Fields AskUserRequestedEvent before the answerer is called, or before a deferred call pauses the run request AskUserAnsweredEvent after it returns, times out, or raises, before the response is checked or the model sees the result request_id, response, timed_out, failed

Both dispatch immediately, so a listener that shows a "waiting for you" state sees the wait start and end in step with the run. When the answerer raises, the answered event carries failed=True and a cancelled response, then the error propagates from the tool call: a ModelRetry sends the model a retry prompt, and any other error fails the run. A run cancelled while the answerer waits emits no answered event, so also clear waiting state when the run ends. Subscribe with @on_event on a capability or through the run's event stream:

from pydantic_ai import RunContext
from pydantic_ai.capabilities import AbstractCapability, on_event

from pydantic_ai_harness.ask_user import AskUserAnsweredEvent, AskUserRequestedEvent


class WaitIndicator(AbstractCapability[None]):
    @on_event(AskUserRequestedEvent)
    async def waiting(self, ctx: RunContext[None], event: AskUserRequestedEvent) -> None:
        print(f'waiting on {len(event.request.questions)} question(s)')

    @on_event(AskUserAnsweredEvent)
    async def done(self, ctx: RunContext[None], event: AskUserAnsweredEvent) -> None:
        if event.failed:
            print('failed')
        elif event.timed_out:
            print('timed out')
        else:
            print('declined' if event.response.cancelled else 'answered')

items.title: What the model sees
items.text:
The tool schema mirrors Code Puppy's ask_user_question, so prompts written for it carry over.

Field Limit questions 1 to 10 per call; headers unique, ignoring case and compatibility forms such as full-width letters header 1 to 25 characters, one line question 1 to 500 characters, may span lines options 2 to 6 per question; labels unique, ignoring case and compatibility forms such as full-width letters label 1 to 50 characters, one line description optional, at most 200 characters, may span lines

These strings are drawn on terminals, where an escape sequence in a prompt-injected call is an attack, so control characters and format characters such as zero-width spaces, joiners and bidirectional overrides are rejected. Spaces of any width are allowed, and uniqueness treats most of them as an ordinary space. A call outside these limits, or with a field the schema does not have, goes back to the model as a validation retry and never reaches the answerer. Once validated the questions are frozen: what the answerer sees is what the model asked.

The result is a JSON object mapping each header to the list of picked labels (or one custom answer), or the sentence The user declined to answer. Continue without the answer, or ask differently if it is essential. When timeout runs out, it is the TIMED_OUT sentence instead.

The capability adds one instruction: ask when the task is ambiguous and the answer is not in the workspace, offer concrete options, batch related questions, and make a stated choice if the user declines.

items.title: One per agent
items.text:
AskUser declares the default id 'ask_user'. The id keys the capability's instructions, so they can be addressed, and lets defer_loading=True work without one. Two AskUsers on one agent that share it are one answerer stated twice: they become one when they agree, and the agent raises a UserError when it's built if they differ. To keep two, give each its own id and wrap them in PrefixTools, since both register ask_user_question. To serve several UIs, pass one answerer that dispatches to them.

Earlier releases declared no default id, so two always failed on the tool name when the run started. Two identical ones now become one, and two that differ fail when the agent is built.

items.title: Tracing
items.text: AskUser emits no spans. Core's tool-call span already covers the wait, and the two events above carry what was asked and answered. That span records the tool's arguments and result, which here are the questions and the user's answers, custom text included. Set include_content=False to leave them out.

items.title: Specs
items.text: Agent.from_spec cannot construct AskUser: the answerer is a live object a spec has no way to name.

items.title: API reference
items.text: check_response, ask_user_result, TOOL_NAME, DECLINED, TIMED_OUT, and MAX_QUESTIONS are also exported from pydantic_ai_harness.ask_user, along with AskUserToolset, the toolset AskUser registers, and ASK_USER_EVENTS, the namespace of both events.

items.title: AWS Lambda Durability
items.text:
এই পেজে যা শিখবেন

  • AWSLambdaDurability দিয়ে একটি এজেন্টকে AWS Lambda durable function-এ আবার-চালু-যোগ্য করা।
  • sync Lambda handler আর async এজেন্ট কীভাবে durable_agent_handler দিয়ে যুক্ত হয়।
  • কী কী checkpoint হয়, step-এর নাম, আর গুরুত্বপূর্ণ সীমাবদ্ধতা (retry, ক্রম, বাজেট)।
  • প্রতি-টুল কনফিগারেশন।

AWSLambdaDurability একটি এজেন্টকে AWS Lambda durable functions-এ আবার-চালু-যোগ্য করে। প্রতিটি মডেল রিকোয়েস্ট, ফাংশন টুল কল, MCP কল আর dynamic-toolset মীমাংসা একটি durable step হিসেবে checkpoint হয়, তাই যে invocation timeout হয়, ব্যর্থ হয় বা retry হয়, তা ইতিমধ্যে টাকা দেওয়া কাজ পুনরাবৃত্তি না করে শেষ সম্পন্ন step থেকে চলতে থাকে।

Lambda durable operation-এর একটি log রাখে। একটি execution আবার চললে, handler আবার শুরু থেকে চলে আর সম্পন্ন step-গুলো চালানোর বদলে তাদের সংরক্ষিত ফল ফেরত দেয়। checkpoint ছাড়া, একটি আবার-চালু রান প্রতিটি মডেল রিকোয়েস্ট আর টুল কল পুনরাবৃত্তি করত।

Pydantic AI Harness 0.x release-এ থাকা অবস্থায়, minor release-এর মধ্যে API বদলাতে পারে; বদলালে, deprecation warning আর release-note-এর migration নির্দেশনা আপনাকে (বা আপনার এজেন্টকে) ঠিক কীভাবে আপগ্রেড করতে হবে তা বলে দেয়। দেখুন version policy।

উদাহরণ দিয়ে বুঝি

একটি Lambda function-এর সর্বোচ্চ চলার সময় সীমিত। ধরুন একটি এজেন্ট ১০টি টুল কল করে আর ৭ নম্বরে timeout হলো। সাধারণ Lambda-য় retry মানে আবার ১ থেকে — আগের ৬টি মডেল কলের টাকা আবার। durable Lambda-য় handler আবার শুরু থেকে চলে, কিন্তু ১-৬ নম্বর step-এর ফল log থেকে সাথে সাথে ফেরত আসে (চলে না), আর কাজ ৭ থেকে এগোয়।

items.title: ইনস্টলেশন
items.text:
pipuv 
pip install "pydantic-ai-harness[aws-lambda]"

uv add "pydantic-ai-harness[aws-lambda]"

AWS Durable Execution SDK-এর জন্য Python 3.11 বা নতুনতর লাগে।

নিচের quick start একটি Bedrock provider মডেল ব্যবহার করে, যার জন্য pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock] থেকে Bedrock SDK লাগে:

pipuv 
pip install "pydantic-ai-harness[aws-lambda]" "pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]"

uv add "pydantic-ai-harness[aws-lambda]" "pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]"

items.title: দ্রুত শুরু
items.text:
এজেন্ট তৈরির সময় capability যুক্ত করুন, তারপর durable_agent_handler দিয়ে একটি async handler body মানিয়ে নিন:

handler.py
from typing import Any

from aws_durable_execution_sdk_python import DurableContext, durable_execution
from pydantic_ai import Agent

from pydantic_ai_harness.aws_lambda import AWSLambdaDurability, durable_agent_handler

agent = Agent(
    'bedrock:global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5',
    name='support',
    capabilities=[AWSLambdaDurability()],
)


@agent.tool_plain
def get_weather(city: str) -> str:
    return f'It is sunny in {city}.'


@durable_execution
@durable_agent_handler
async def handler(event: dict[str, Any], context: DurableContext) -> str:
    result = await agent.run(str(event['prompt']))
    return result.output

প্রতি রানে না করে তৈরির সময় capability যুক্ত করুন। প্রতি-রানে যুক্ত করাও কাজ করে (capability যেকোনোভাবেই toolset বাঁধে আর মোড়ায়), কিন্তু একবার যুক্ত করলে মোড়ানো আর deploy করা step-এর রূপ invocation জুড়ে স্থিতিশীল থাকে, আর এটি অন্য durability ইন্টিগ্রেশনের সাথে মেলে।

একটি durable কনফিগারেশন দিয়ে deploy করুন আর একটি published version invoke করুন, কারণ চলমান execution তাদের শুরু করা version-এ আটকানো থাকে:

aws lambda create-function \
  --function-name support-agent \
  --runtime python3.13 \
  --handler handler.handler \
  --role <ROLE_ARN> \
  --zip-file fileb://support-agent.zip \
  --timeout 300 --memory-size 1024 \
  --durable-config '{"ExecutionTimeout":3600,"RetentionPeriodInDays":7}'

aws lambda publish-version --function-name support-agent

একটি রান শুধু durable handler সেতুর ভেতরেই durable

AWSLambdaDurability যুক্ত করা নিজে থেকে একটি রান durable করে না। শুধু durable_agent_handler বা run_durable দিয়ে প্রবেশ করা একটি রানই checkpoint হয়। agent.run_sync(...) ডাকা, বা নিজের asyncio.run(...) থেকে এজেন্ট await করা, একটি পুরোপুরি কাজ করা কিন্তু non-durable রান তৈরি করে, কোনো সতর্কবার্তা ছাড়াই।

items.title: প্রয়োজনীয়তা
items.text: এজেন্টের একটি name (বা AWSLambdaDurability(name=...)) লাগে, আর প্রতিটি পাতা-স্তরের toolset-এর একটি অনন্য id লাগে। দুটোই প্রতিটি step নামের অংশ, তাই এজেন্ট তৈরির সময়ই দুটো যাচাই হয়: নাম ছাড়া একটি এজেন্ট Agent(...) থেকে একটি UserError তোলে, একইভাবে id নেই বা অন্য toolset-এর সাথে একই id ভাগ করা একটি toolset-ও। এজেন্টে সরাসরি নিবন্ধিত টুল এমন একটি toolset-এ থাকে যার id <agent> হিসেবে দেখায়, তাই @agent.tool_plain def get_weather checkpoint হয় {name}__function_toolset__<agent>.call_tool:get_weather হিসেবে।

items.title: sync handler আর async এজেন্ট কীভাবে যুক্ত হয়
items.text:
Lambda-র durable API synchronous: context.step(...) আটকে থাকে, আর প্রতিটি step Lambda যে thread invoke করেছে তাতেই তৈরি করতে হয়। একটি এজেন্ট রান async। durable_agent_handler দুটিকে জুড়তে run_durable ব্যবহার করে: এটি async handler body একটি background event loop-এ রাখে আর এর step-গুলো Lambda handler thread-এ পরিবেশন করে, তাই সব step একটি অবিচ্ছিন্ন ক্রমে তৈরি হয়। একটি step body এর কাজ এজেন্ট loop-এ ফেরত দেয় আর শেষ না হওয়া পর্যন্ত আটকে থাকে, যা handler thread অপেক্ষার সময় loop-কে মুক্ত রাখে।

async body কয়েকটি এজেন্ট রান await করতে পারে আর তাদের মাঝে async কাজ করতে পারে, আর ওই সব অংশ একই সেতু আর step ক্রম ভাগ করে। রানগুলো একটার পর একটা await করুন, asyncio.gather বা task দিয়ে একসাথে নয়: একটি আবার-চালু execution checkpoint মেলায় step-গুলো যে ক্রমে পৌঁছানো হয় তা দিয়ে, তাই replay-তে ভিন্ন ক্রমে তাদের step-এ পৌঁছানো একসাথে চলা রানগুলো একে অপরের লেখা ফল পায়। একটি synchronous handler-কে প্রতিটি async অংশের জন্য আলাদাভাবে run_durable ডাকতে হয়, আর একসাথে কল প্রত্যাখ্যাত হয়।

তিনটি ফলাফল জানা মূল্যবান:

  • @durable_execution অবশ্যই সবচেয়ে বাইরের decorator হতে হবে, কারণ এর wrapper-ই Lambda invoke করে। ক্রম উল্টালে handler সংজ্ঞায়িত হওয়ার সময় একটি UserError ওঠে।
  • run_durable ডাকা thread আটকে রাখে, তাই একটি চলমান event loop-এর ভেতর থেকে এটি ডাকা যায় না। একটি synchronous handler থেকে সরাসরি এটি ডাকুন। সেতুতে একটি handler-এর শীর্ষ ছাড়া অন্য কোথাও প্রবেশ করতে হলে এটি উপলব্ধ থাকে।
  • Durable step nest করতে পারে না। আরেকটি durable এজেন্ট রান শুরু করা একটি টুল deadlock না করে একটি ব্যাখ্যামূলক error দিয়ে প্রত্যাখ্যাত হয়।

একটি উষ্ণ execution environment-এর invocation জুড়ে loop পুনর্ব্যবহৃত হয়, তাই একটি provider-এর cache করা HTTP client-এর মতো loop-বাঁধা resource তাদের মাঝে বৈধ থাকে। তাই একটি স্থগিত বা error-এ পরিত্যক্ত রান handler ফেরত দেওয়ার আগে বাতিল হয়, আর run_durable এটি গুটিয়ে নেওয়ার জন্য cancel_timeout সেকেন্ড (ডিফল্ট 5) অপেক্ষা করে। যে কাজের পরিষ্কার সত্যিই ধীর, তার জন্য এটি বাড়ান। timeout শেষ হলে, পরিত্যক্ত পরিষ্কার-কাজ একটি অবসরপ্রাপ্ত loop-এ সর্বোচ্চ সেই loop-এর grace period পর্যন্ত চলতে থাকে আর পরের উষ্ণ invocation-এর সাথে মিশে যেতে পারে। এজেন্ট রান আর handler-এর মধ্যে পরিবর্তনযোগ্য module-global state ভাগ করবেন না। পরিষ্কার-কাজের একটি বাইরের side effect, যেমন একটি store-এ লেখা, একটি ভাগ করা lock ছাড়া, বা একটি metric পাঠানো, পরের একটি invocation-এর সময়ও ঘটতে পারে। Loop-বাঁধা resource বিচ্ছিন্ন: পরের invocation একটি নতুন loop পায়, তাই পরিত্যক্ত পরিষ্কার-কাজ ওই invocation-এর provider HTTP client-এর মতো resource ছুঁতে পারে না।

loop পুনর্ব্যবহারের আরও একটি ফলাফল আছে: একটি টুল থেকে asyncio.create_task() দিয়ে বা executor কাজ await না করে রেখে background কাজ আলাদা করবেন না। আলাদা করা কাজ checkpoint হয় না আর durable execution-এর নিশ্চয়তায় কভার হয় না, আর এটি একে শুরু করা invocation-এর চেয়ে বেশি দিন টিকতে পারে।

items.title: কী checkpoint হয়
items.text:
Step-এর নাম তৈরি হয় এজেন্টের name আর প্রতিটি toolset-এর id থেকে:

Step-এর নাম কাজ {name}__model.request একটি মডেল রিকোয়েস্ট অংশ {name}__model.request_stream একটি stream করা মডেল রিকোয়েস্ট অংশ {name}__model.compact_messages একটি মডেল message-compaction কাজ {name}__model.cancel_suspended_response একটি স্থগিত response গুটিয়ে ফেলা {name}__capability__{capability_id}.{operation} অন্য একটি capability-র দেওয়া একটি কাজ {name}__function_toolset__{id}.validate_args একটি ফাংশন টুল কলের আর্গুমেন্ট যাচাই {name}__function_toolset__{id}.call_tool:{tool} একটি ফাংশন টুল কল {name}__mcp_server__{id}.get_tools একটি MCP সার্ভারের টুল তালিকা {name}__mcp_server__{id}.get_instructions একটি MCP সার্ভারের instructions {name}__mcp_server__{id}.call_tool একটি MCP টুল কল {name}__dynamic_toolset__{id}.get_tools একটি dynamic toolset মীমাংসা {name}__dynamic_toolset__{id}.validate_args একটি dynamic toolset কলের আর্গুমেন্ট যাচাই {name}__dynamic_toolset__{id}.call_tool:{tool} একটি dynamic toolset-এর টুল কল {name}__event_stream_handler একটি event_stream_handler-এ পাঠানো একটি event

এজেন্টের ডিফল্ট মডেল ব্যবহার করে না এমন একটি মডেল কাজ step নামে এর model id লেখে (যেমন {name}__model.request.{model_id}), তাই execution history দেখায় প্রতিটি checkpoint কোন মডেল থেকে এসেছে। ডিফল্ট মডেল সাধারণ, প্রত্যয়-ছাড়া নাম রাখে।

items.title: সীমাবদ্ধতা
items.text:
• Step অন্তত একবার চলে, আর ডিফল্টভাবে retry হয়। একটি step চলার পরে checkpoint হয়, তাই একটি টুলের side effect আর এর checkpoint-এর মাঝে একটি বাধা execution আবার চলার সময় টুলটি আবার চালায়। এর ওপরে, SDK-এর ডিফল্ট retry policy হলো exponential backoff-সহ (5s থেকে 60s) ছয়টি চেষ্টা, প্রতিটি মডেল রিকোয়েস্ট আর প্রতিটি টুল কলে প্রযোজ্য। টুলের side effect idempotent রাখুন। শুধু AT_MOST_ONCE_PER_RETRY একটি টুলকে একবার চালাতে যথেষ্ট নয়: এটি একটি চেষ্টার ভেতরে একটি বাধার পর আবার চালানো আটকায়, কিন্তু retry policy তবুও আরও চেষ্টা শুরু করে যা body চালায়। যে টুল পুনরাবৃত্তি করা চলবে না, তার জন্য দুটোই সেট করুন:

    from aws_durable_execution_sdk_python.config import StepSemantics
from aws_durable_execution_sdk_python.retries import RetryPresets

metadata={'aws_lambda': {'step_semantics': StepSemantics.AT_MOST_ONCE_PER_RETRY,
                         'retry_strategy': RetryPresets.none()}}

  • Retry জমা হয়। Pydantic AI আর provider client-এর নিজস্ব retry লজিক আছে। step retry policy-র পাশাপাশি সেগুলো চালু রাখলে চেষ্টার সংখ্যা গুণিত হয় আর Retry-After ভুলভাবে সামলানো হয়; একটি দিক বন্ধ করুন।

  • টুল কল একবারে একটি চলে। একটি step-এর পরিচয় আসে step-গুলো যে ক্রমে পৌঁছানো হয় তা থেকে, তাই একসাথে নির্ধারিত টুল কল execution আবার চলার সময় একে অপরের checkpoint দাবি করতে পারত। একটি durable handler-এর ভেতরে রান ক্রমিক টুল চালানোয় বদলে যায়। এর বাইরে এজেন্ট তার কনফিগার করা সমান্তরালতা রাখে।
  • রানের রূপ বদলালে চলমান execution ভাঙে। একটি আবার-চালু execution step নাম দিয়ে নয়, কাজগুলো যে ক্রমে পৌঁছানো হয় তা দিয়ে checkpoint মেলায়, তাই step-এর সংখ্যা বা ক্রম বদলায় এমন যেকোনো কিছু পুরনো কোডে শুরু হওয়া execution ভাঙে: একটি টুল বা MCP সার্ভার যোগ বা বাদ দেওয়া, একটি metadata={'aws_lambda': False} opt-out উল্টানো, বা একটি event_stream_handler যোগ করা (যা model step-কে model.request_stream-এ বদলায় আর handler step যোগ করে)। অমিল ধরা পড়ে না: একটি step আরেকটি step-এর লেখা ফল পায়, যা সাধারণত decode হতে ব্যর্থ হয় কিন্তু নিঃশব্দে ভুল ডেটাও ফেরত দিতে পারে। একটি নতুন published version-এ deploy করুন আর চলমান execution পুরনোটিতে শেষ হতে দিন।
  • Step-এর ফল SDK serializer-এ টিকতে হবে। ফল Lambda SDK-এর serializer দিয়ে checkpoint হয়। টুলের ফল আগে Pydantic দিয়ে encode হয়, তাই ToolReturn আর BinaryContent-এর মতো কাঠামোবদ্ধ ফেরত যাওয়া-আসা করে; Pydantic serialize করতে পারে না এমন একটি মান পারে না।
  • একটি চলমান durable execution থেকে event বেরোতে পারে না। run_stream আর iter handler-এর ভেতরে কাজ করে আর স্বাভাবিকভাবে checkpoint হয়, কিন্তু একটি durable execution শেষ হলে একটি একক মান ফেরত দেয়, তাই চলার সময় একজন caller-এর কাছে token stream করার কোনো চ্যানেল নেই। একটি event_stream_handler কাজ করে: মডেল event model step-এর ভেতরে লাইভ সামলানো হয় আর প্রতিটি এজেন্ট-স্তরের event নিজের step-এ checkpoint হয়।
  • একটি durable step-এর ভেতরে ctx.enqueue() পাওয়া যায় না, একটি checkpoint করা টুল হোক বা একটি event_stream_handler (যা মডেল event-এর জন্য model step-এর ভেতরে আর এজেন্ট event-এর জন্য নিজের step-এ চলে), কারণ একটি আবার-চালু execution লেখা step আউটপুট পরিবেশন করে আর enqueue করা বার্তা হারিয়ে যেত। এর বদলে handler-স্তরের কোড থেকে enqueue করুন।
  • Checkpoint রানের ডেটা রাখে। মডেল response, টুলের ফল, আর ব্যর্থ step-এর error বার্তা (যাতে একটি provider-এর error response body থাকতে পারে) durable কনফিগারেশনের RetentionPeriodInDays পর্যন্ত execution-এর durable state-এ সংরক্ষিত থাকে। execution history পড়তে পারা যে কেউ এগুলো পড়তে পারে, তাই সংবেদনশীল কাজের জন্য retention period ছোট রাখুন।
  • বাজেট। একটি durable execution 3,000টি কাজ আর 100 MB মোট checkpoint করা state অনুমতি দেয়। একটি turn-এর খরচ একটি model step আর প্রতি টুল কলে একটি step, তাই কাজের বাজেট উদার, কিন্তু বড় টুলের ফল state বাজেট খায়: একটি blob-এর বদলে একটি রেফারেন্স (ধরুন একটি S3 key) ফেরত দিন।

সাধারণ ভুল

একটি charge_card টুলে শুধু step_semantics=AT_MOST_ONCE_PER_RETRY দিয়ে ভাবা যে কার্ডে একবারই চার্জ হবে। ডিফল্ট retry policy ছয়বার পর্যন্ত চেষ্টা করে — প্রতিটি নতুন চেষ্টায় টুল আবার চলে। একবারই চালাতে হলে ওপরের উদাহরণের মতো retry_strategy-তেও RetryPresets.none() দিন, আর সাথে payment API-তে idempotency key ব্যবহার করুন।

items.title: প্রতি-টুল কনফিগারেশন
items.text:
aws_lambda key-র নিচে টুলের metadata সেই টুলের step কনফিগার করে। এটি StepConfig-এর retry_strategy, step_semantics আর serdes ফিল্ড নেয়:

from aws_durable_execution_sdk_python.config import StepSemantics
from pydantic_ai.toolsets import FunctionToolset

toolset = FunctionToolset(id='billing')


@toolset.tool_plain(metadata={'aws_lambda': {'step_semantics': StepSemantics.AT_MOST_ONCE_PER_RETRY}})
def charge_card(amount: int) -> str:
    return f'charged {amount}'

metadata={'aws_lambda': False} একটি টুলকে checkpoint থেকে পুরোপুরি বের করে, তাই এটি প্রতিটি চেষ্টায় inline চলে। এটি ব্যবহার করুন সস্তা, side-effect-মুক্ত টুলের জন্য, যার ফল একটি checkpoint-এর যোগ্য নয়। MCP টুল বেরোতে পারে না, কারণ এগুলো এমন I/O করে যা execution আবার চলার সময় আবার চলা উচিত নয়।

AWSLambdaDurability(step_config=...) প্রতিটি step-এর মূল কনফিগারেশন সেট করে। প্রতি-টুল metadata এটি key ধরে ধরে override করে, তাই শুধু step_semantics সেট করা একটি টুল মূল retry_strategy রাখে।

items.title: অন্য capability-র সাথে মিলন
items.text: AWSLambdaDurability নিজেকে সবচেয়ে ভেতরে রাখে, তাই একটি মডেল রিকোয়েস্টে অন্য যেকোনো capability-র অবদান durable step-এর ভেতরে আগেই প্রয়োগ হয়ে যায়। অন্য capability-র পাশে স্বাভাবিকভাবে এটি যুক্ত করুন।

items.text:
সংক্ষেপে মনে রাখুন

  • Agent(name=..., capabilities=[AWSLambdaDurability()]) আর handler @durable_execution + durable_agent_handler দিয়ে।
  • শুধু durable_agent_handler/run_durable দিয়ে প্রবেশ করা রানই durable; run_sync() নিঃশব্দে non-durable।
  • @durable_execution সবচেয়ে বাইরের decorator; একাধিক রান একটার পর একটা await করুন।
  • step অন্তত-একবার আর ডিফল্টভাবে 6 বার পর্যন্ত retry — টুল idempotent রাখুন।
  • টুল বা MCP যোগ/বাদ দিলে চলমান execution ভাঙে — নতুন published version-এ deploy করুন।
  • বাজেট: 3,000 কাজ, 100 MB state; বড় ফলের বদলে S3 key ফেরত দিন।

items.text:
AWSLambdaDurability(
    *,
    models=None,
    event_stream_handler=None,
    name=None,
    step_config=None
)

Bases: BaseDurabilityCapability[AgentDepsT]

Capability that checkpoints an agent's I/O into AWS Lambda durable steps.

Attach it with capabilities=[AWSLambdaDurability()] and decorate an async handler with durable_agent_handler: every model request, function tool call, MCP call, and dynamic-toolset resolution is wrapped in DurableContext.step(...). A completed step is served from its checkpoint when the execution resumes, so finished work is not repeated and tokens are not re-spent.

A step is checkpointed after it runs, so an interruption between a tool's side effect and its checkpoint re-runs the tool when the execution resumes: keep tool side effects idempotent, or set step_semantics to AT_MOST_ONCE_PER_RETRY for the tools that cannot tolerate it.

Outside a durable handler the capability is transparent and the run is an ordinary agent run.

Step results are checkpointed through the Lambda SDK's serializer, so a checkpointed tool's return value must survive that round trip. Control-flow signals (ModelRetry, ApprovalRequired, CallDeferred, ToolFailed) cross the boundary as values rather than exceptions, so approval and deferred-tool flows work inside a durable execution.

Example 
from aws_durable_execution_sdk_python import DurableContext, durable_execution
from pydantic_ai import Agent
from pydantic_ai_harness.aws_lambda import AWSLambdaDurability, durable_agent_handler

agent = Agent('bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0', name='support', capabilities=[AWSLambdaDurability()])


@agent.tool_plain
def get_weather(city: str) -> str:
    return f'It is sunny in {city}.'


@durable_execution
@durable_agent_handler
async def handler(event: dict[str, object], context: DurableContext) -> str:
    result = await agent.run(str(event['prompt']))
    return result.output

The agent's model, name, and toolsets are discovered when the capability is bound.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION models

Optional additional models keyed by ID for run-time model switching via agent.run(model='<id>'). The ID is folded into the step name so a resumed execution maps each checkpoint back to the model it was recorded for.

TYPE: Mapping[str, Model] | None DEFAULT: None

event_stream_handler

Optional event stream handler. Model events are handled live inside the model-request step; each agent-level event is handled in its own checkpointed step.

TYPE: EventStreamHandler[AgentDepsT] | None DEFAULT: None

name

Unique agent name used as the prefix for every step name. Defaults to the agent's name when the capability is bound.

TYPE: str | None DEFAULT: None

step_config

Base StepConfig fields applied to every step, as a mapping of retry_strategy, step_semantics, and serdes. Per-tool metadata={'aws_lambda': {...}} overrides it key by key for that tool.

TYPE: Mapping[str, Any] | None DEFAULT: None

Source code in pydantic_ai_harness/aws_lambda/_capability.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    models: Mapping[str, Model] | None = None,
    event_stream_handler: EventStreamHandler[AgentDepsT] | None = None,
    name: str | None = None,
    step_config: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Create an `AWSLambdaDurability` capability.

    The agent's model, name, and toolsets are discovered when the capability is bound.

    Args:
        models: Optional additional models keyed by ID for run-time model switching via
            `agent.run(model='<id>')`. The ID is folded into the step name so a resumed
            execution maps each checkpoint back to the model it was recorded for.
        event_stream_handler: Optional event stream handler. Model events are handled live
            inside the model-request step; each agent-level event is handled in its own
            checkpointed step.
        name: Unique agent name used as the prefix for every step name. Defaults to the
            agent's `name` when the capability is bound.
        step_config: Base `StepConfig` fields applied to every step, as a mapping of
            `retry_strategy`, `step_semantics`, and `serdes`. Per-tool
            `metadata={'aws_lambda': {...}}` overrides it key by key for that tool.
    """
    super().__init__(models=models, event_stream_handler=event_stream_handler, name=name)
    self._operation_config = AWSLambdaOperationConfig(step_config)

Adapt an async handler body for the AWS durable execution decorator.

@durable_execution must be outermost because its synchronous wrapper is what Lambda invokes.

Example 
@durable_execution
@durable_agent_handler
async def handler(event: dict[str, Any], context: DurableContext) -> str:
    result = await agent.run(event['prompt'])
    return result.output
PARAMETER DESCRIPTION func

Async durable handler body.

TYPE: Callable[[Any, DurableStepContext], Coroutine[Any, Any, T]] | None DEFAULT: None

cancel_timeout

Seconds to wait for an abandoned handler body to unwind. See run_durable.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: DEFAULT_CANCEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS

Source code in pydantic_ai_harness/aws_lambda/_bridge.py 
def durable_agent_handler(
    func: Callable[[Any, DurableStepContext], Coroutine[Any, Any, T]] | None = None,
    /,
    *,
    cancel_timeout: float = DEFAULT_CANCEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
) -> (
    Callable[[Any, DurableStepContext], T]
    | Callable[
        [Callable[[Any, DurableStepContext], Coroutine[Any, Any, T]]],
        Callable[[Any, DurableStepContext], T],
    ]
):
    """Adapt an async handler body for the AWS durable execution decorator.

    `@durable_execution` must be outermost because its synchronous wrapper is what Lambda invokes.

    Example:
        ```python {test="skip"}
        @durable_execution
        @durable_agent_handler
        async def handler(event: dict[str, Any], context: DurableContext) -> str:
            result = await agent.run(event['prompt'])
            return result.output
        ```

    Args:
        func: Async durable handler body.
        cancel_timeout: Seconds to wait for an abandoned handler body to unwind. See `run_durable`.
    """

    def decorate(
        handler: Callable[[Any, DurableStepContext], Coroutine[Any, Any, T]],
    ) -> Callable[[Any, DurableStepContext], T]:
        if not inspect.iscoroutinefunction(handler):
            raise UserError(
                '`@durable_agent_handler` requires an async handler. `@durable_execution` must be the '
                'outermost decorator because it is what Lambda invokes. A synchronous handler should '
                'call `run_durable` directly instead.'
            )

        @functools.wraps(handler)
        def wrapped(event: Any, context: DurableStepContext) -> T:
            return run_durable(lambda: handler(event, context), context=context, cancel_timeout=cancel_timeout)

        return wrapped

    if func is None:
        return decorate
    return decorate(func)

items.title: pydantic_ai_harness.aws_lambda.run_durable
items.text:
run_durable(
    agent_run,
    *,
    context,
    cancel_timeout=DEFAULT_CANCEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
)

Run an async agent call from a synchronous Lambda durable handler.

Hosts agent_run() on a background event loop and services its durable steps on the calling (handler) thread, so every context.step(...) is created in one continuous sequence on the thread Lambda invoked. Returns whatever agent_run() returns.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION agent_run

Callable returning the coroutine to run, e.g. lambda: agent.run(prompt). It is called once per handler invocation, including each replay.

TYPE: Callable[[], Coroutine[Any, Any, T]]

context

The DurableContext the durable handler was invoked with.

TYPE: DurableStepContext

cancel_timeout

Seconds to wait for a run abandoned by a suspension or an error to finish unwinding before returning. Raise it for a workload whose cleanup is genuinely slow. When it expires, the background event loop is retired so the next invocation builds a fresh loop and the cleanup cannot touch its loop-bound resources, such as a provider's cached HTTP client. The cleanup can still run during that invocation for the retired loop's grace period, so it can still affect module-global state or external systems.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: DEFAULT_CANCEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS

Example 
@durable_execution
def handler(event: dict[str, Any], context: DurableContext) -> str:
    result = run_durable(lambda: agent.run(event['prompt']), context=context)
    return result.output
Source code in pydantic_ai_harness/aws_lambda/_bridge.py 
def run_durable(
    agent_run: Callable[[], Coroutine[Any, Any, T]],
    *,
    context: DurableStepContext,
    cancel_timeout: float = DEFAULT_CANCEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
) -> T:
    """Run an async agent call from a synchronous Lambda durable handler.

    Hosts `agent_run()` on a background event loop and services its durable steps on the calling
    (handler) thread, so every `context.step(...)` is created in one continuous sequence on the
    thread Lambda invoked. Returns whatever `agent_run()` returns.

    Args:
        agent_run: Callable returning the coroutine to run, e.g. `lambda: agent.run(prompt)`.
            It is called once per handler invocation, including each replay.
        context: The `DurableContext` the durable handler was invoked with.
        cancel_timeout: Seconds to wait for a run abandoned by a suspension or an error to finish
            unwinding before returning. Raise it for a workload whose cleanup is genuinely slow.
            When it expires, the background event loop is retired so the next invocation builds a
            fresh loop and the cleanup cannot touch its loop-bound resources, such as a provider's
            cached HTTP client. The cleanup can still run during that invocation for the retired
            loop's grace period, so it can still affect module-global state or external systems.

    Example:
        ```python {test="skip"}
        @durable_execution
        def handler(event: dict[str, Any], context: DurableContext) -> str:
            result = run_durable(lambda: agent.run(event['prompt']), context=context)
            return result.output
        ```
    """
    try:
        asyncio.get_running_loop()
    except RuntimeError:
        pass
    else:
        raise UserError(
            '`run_durable()` blocks the calling thread until the agent run finishes, so it cannot be '
            f'called from a running event loop. An {ENGINE_NAME} durable handler is synchronous, so '
            'call it directly from the handler; if you already have an event loop, await the agent '
            'run instead.'
        )
    if _active_bridge.get() is not None:
        raise UserError(
            f'`run_durable()` is already active on this thread. An {ENGINE_NAME} durable handler runs '
            'one agent run at a time; call `run_durable()` once per handler invocation.'
        )
    if not _active_run.acquire(blocking=False):
        raise UserError(
            f'`run_durable()` is already active on another thread. An {ENGINE_NAME} execution '
            'environment has one shared agent event loop, so concurrent handler calls are unsafe.'
        )
    try:
        return _run_durable_on_agent_loop(agent_run, context=context, cancel_timeout=cancel_timeout)
    finally:
        _active_run.release()

items.title: pydantic_ai_harness.aws_lambda.AgentLoopGone
items.text:
Bases: BaseException

The agent loop stopped while a durable step was in flight, so its result can never arrive.

A BaseException rather than an Exception on purpose: consume() routes ordinary step failures back into the agent run so it can handle them, and that is precisely what cannot work here -- the loop that would receive them is the thing that is gone. Like the SDK's own control flow, this has to leave the handler instead.
