items.text:
Feature Support Notes Audio format Limited parameter support Mono PCM16, 24 kHz input and output; the API also offers 8 kHz G.711, which Pydantic AI does not expose Text output Full feature support Select with output_modality='text' Image input Full feature support Images provide context for the next turn Manual turns Full feature support turn_detection=False plus commit/create verbs Interruption/truncation Full feature support interrupt(played_ms=...) records the heard cutoff Input transcription Limited parameter support Requires a compatible transcription deployment in the Azure resource Native tools Unsupported The API offers remote MCP servers (plus Foundry tools and agents on Voice Live) but no web or file search; Pydantic AI doesn't expose the MCP support yet (#9032), so configure local fallbacks Browser WebRTC Limited parameter support GA only Usage Full feature support Token, audio, and cache breakdowns Reconnection Full feature support Pydantic AI replays completed local history; in-flight media is lost

See Audio, images, and transcripts, Turns and interruptions, Tools, and Connection lifecycle for the provider-agnostic workflows.

items.title: Provider-specific quirks
items.text:
• A failed input transcription leaves the user turn represented as retained audio when available, or as a content-less SpeechPart otherwise.
  • Azure AI Voice Live rides the same model behind azure_voice_live=True, against its own resource and beta session protocol; browser WebRTC is GA-only for now.
  • Voice Live's informational warning events are raised as Python UserWarnings, so escalating warnings to errors ends the session.
  • Voice Live closes the connection right after a session_output_overflow error, which it can send during a long spoken reply. Without a reconnect policy, the error is reported as a non-recoverable RealtimeSessionErrorEvent and the session raises a RealtimeError; with one, the error is recoverable and the session reconnects.

items.title: Capabilities and hooks
items.text:
🌐 এই পেজের সহজ বাংলা সংস্করণ এখনো তৈরি হচ্ছে

আপাতত নিচে মূল ইংরেজি লেখাটি দেখানো হচ্ছে। এই অংশের অন্য পেজগুলোতে সহজ বাংলা ব্যাখ্যা পাবেন।

অফিসিয়াল ইংরেজি পেজ

items.title: Capabilities and hooks
items.text: A capability attached to the agent or passed to realtime(capabilities=...) participates in a realtime session where its lifecycle maps onto a persistent connection. Third-party capabilities load exactly the same way as in a regular run; nothing realtime-specific is required of them.

items.title: Capability stages in a session
items.text:
Capability stage Session behavior for_agent, for_run, get_instructions Runs during setup; dynamic instructions are evaluated once at connect. get_toolset, get_wrapper_toolset, prepare_tools Contributes, wraps, and prepares local tools before connecting. get_native_tools Contributes native tools before connecting; a dynamic native-tool function is resolved once against the connect-time context, like dynamic instructions. Tool validation/execution hooks Runs around each local function-tool call. handle_deferred_tool_calls Resolves deferred requests inline; see deferred and approval-required tools. Graph node, model-request, and output-processing hooks Do not run; no agent graph or output-processing stage exists.

All regular tool validation and tool execution hooks — before, after, wrap, and on_error for both stages — run around every local function-tool call exactly as in a standard run, retries and all. What does not run is anything tied to the request-response graph: node hooks, model request hooks such as before_model_request, and output validation and output processing hooks — a session has no graph nodes, no per-request boundary, and no output stage.

Opening a session emits a UserWarning for each capability that implements any of those hooks, naming the capability and its hooks, since what it does there won't happen in the session — for example, ReinjectSystemPrompt works through before_model_request. A Hooks capability warns only for the hooks it registers. Built-ins whose behavior the session provides another way, such as Instrumentation, don't warn.

items.title: Run hooks
items.text: before_run, after_run, wrap_run, and on_run_error run hooks run once around the session — a realtime session is a run — with the same close-boundary recovery and result-transformation semantics as iter().

items.title: The event stream
items.text: wrap_run_event_stream wraps the consumer-facing session iterator. It can observe or transform shared AgentStreamEvent members and realtime-only RealtimeSessionEvent members (see the event reference) without changing history or tool execution. There is no event_stream_handler parameter on realtime(); a handler-style consumer is attached with the ProcessEventStream capability, which works through this same stream.

items.title: Model settings and RunContext
items.text:
get_model_settings() may run during capability setup, but regular model settings do not configure a realtime model. Pass RealtimeModelSettings through realtime(model_settings=...) instead. Inside session hooks and tools, the RunContext reflects the session:

RunContext field Value in a realtime session ctx.model_settings The merged RealtimeModelSettings the session was connected with. ctx.realtime True for the whole run, including for_run and instruction functions that run before the connection exists. ctx.realtime_session The live RealtimeSession in tool and on_event contexts; None in run hooks.

Note

ctx.realtime_session is None throughout wrap_run, both before and after handler(), because the hook keeps the context copy captured before the session exists. It is also None in before_run and instruction functions. Use tool hooks or on_event when a capability needs the live session.

items.title: Seeded history is not processed
items.text: History-processing capabilities do not transform message_history before it is seeded into a session; preprocess the history before opening the session when filtering or redaction is required.

items.title: Deferred capability loading
items.text: Deferred capabilities load in a session the same way they do in a regular run: the capability catalog is part of the session's instructions, and calling the load_capability tool returns the loaded capability's instructions as its result — which works on every provider. What a session cannot do yet is advertise new tools mid-conversation: Pydantic AI fixes the connection's tools when it opens (OpenAI and xAI accept a mid-session tool update; #7288), so opening a session with a defer_loading=True capability that contributes tools or native tools raises UserError before connecting — accepting it would silently provide less than requested. Loading those tools on providers that accept the update is tracked in #7191.

items.title: Connecting a frontend
items.text:
🌐 এই পেজের সহজ বাংলা সংস্করণ এখনো তৈরি হচ্ছে

আপাতত নিচে মূল ইংরেজি লেখাটি দেখানো হচ্ছে। এই অংশের অন্য পেজগুলোতে সহজ বাংলা ব্যাখ্যা পাবেন।

অফিসিয়াল ইংরেজি পেজ

items.title: Connecting a frontend
items.text:
Keep provider keys, tools, and business logic on the server; connect user devices to your backend, not straight to the provider. How audio travels between the device and the model depends on the client and the provider:

  • Browser WebRTC + server sideband — the recommended browser path on OpenAI and Azure OpenAI: the browser exchanges media directly with the provider (lowest latency) while your backend runs the agent over a control-plane sideband.
  • Browser → backend WebSocket relay — works with every provider, including Gemini Live, xAI, and ElevenLabs Agents: the browser streams audio to your backend, which owns the media bridge.
  • SIP / telephony bridge — for phone calls, via a telephony provider.

In every setup the session — with its tools, history, and usage limits — runs on your backend. Wiring a browser straight to the provider with the provider's own SDK instead moves the agent loop into the client and gives up all of that; prefer one of the setups above.

items.title: Browser WebRTC + server sideband
items.text:
For browser voice agents on OpenAI and Azure OpenAI, the browser carries microphone and speaker audio directly over WebRTC while the backend attaches a control-plane sideband to the same call. Media never touches your backend, so latency stays low, while tools, history, dependencies, and provider credentials stay on the server. Gemini Live, xAI, and ElevenLabs Agents do not offer this sideband transport — use the WebSocket relay there.

browser ── WebRTC media ── provider
   │                         ▲
   └─ SDP offer → backend ───┘ sideband identified by call_id

Relay the browser's offer with AgentRealtime.answer_webrtc_offer, return the SDP answer to the browser, then attach the returned call handle:

import asyncio

from pydantic_ai import Agent

agent = Agent(instructions='You are a concise voice assistant.')
realtime = agent.realtime('openai:gpt-realtime-2.1')
sideband_tasks: set[asyncio.Task[None]] = set()


async def handle_offer(sdp_offer: str) -> str:
    answer = await realtime.answer_webrtc_offer(sdp_offer)

    async def run_sideband() -> None:
        async with realtime.session(provider_session=answer.session) as session:
            async for event in session:
                print(event)

    task = asyncio.create_task(run_sideband())
    sideband_tasks.add(task)  # (1)!
    task.add_done_callback(sideband_tasks.discard)
    return answer.sdp
  1. asyncio keeps only a weak reference to a task, so hold one yourself until the call ends; the done callback also surfaces an error the sideband session raised instead of leaving it as a "never retrieved" warning.

The secure offer-relay flow never gives the browser a token. As an alternative, AgentRealtime.create_client_secret mints a short-lived credential for client-led negotiation: the browser posts its offer to the secret's webrtc_url with the secret as its bearer token. Either way the browser is a peer on the provider session and can send provider-native control events, so authorize every server-side tool against trusted deps, not session instructions supplied to the model.

To continue an earlier conversation, create the AgentRealtime per call inside the offer handler, realtime = agent.realtime(model, message_history=...), and answer the offer and open the sideband from that same object. GPT-Live takes the history when the offer starts the call, and a sideband opened with other history refuses to attach; the other providers seed it when the sideband attaches.

The browser can read seeded history

Seeding a WebRTC call with message_history sends those prior turns into the shared provider conversation that the browser is a peer on, so a call participant can read them — including confidential tool results — over the data channel (Azure's webrtcfilter=on still forwards conversation-item events). Only seed a call with history that is safe for the browser to see; keep confidential context in deps and tool logic instead.

A sideband does not own the audio transport: its send_audio(), commit_audio(), clear_audio(), and stream_audio() methods raise, and audio_retention must remain 'transcript_only'. Enable input transcription when user speech must appear in history. On gpt-realtime and Azure OpenAI, use RealtimeOutputSpeechStartEvent / RealtimeOutputSpeechEndEvent for speaking indicators, and interrupt() clears the provider's outbound WebRTC audio buffer so barge-in stops playback. GPT-Live emits neither event and doesn't support interrupt() (see its feature support). A dropped sideband follows the same reconnect rules (except on GPT-Live, whose sideband is not reconnected), with one wrinkle covered there: a clean close is treated as the browser hanging up.

Closing a sideband session, or leaving its async with block, only detaches your server: the browser's call stays up, and billed, until the browser hangs up. To end the call from the server, call hang_up() instead (it works from a tool too), or hang_up(answer.session) on agent.realtime(model) when no sideband is attached. OpenAI supports this for both gpt-realtime and GPT-Live, and so does Azure OpenAI.

The realtime WebRTC example demonstrates the full FastAPI and browser flow. Provider-specific setup (Azure's Microsoft Entra ID and webrtcfilter) lives on the Azure page.

items.title: Browser → backend WebSocket relay
items.text:
When the browser can't use WebRTC — or the provider is Gemini Live, xAI, or ElevenLabs Agents — build a WebSocket endpoint on your backend that accepts the browser's microphone audio and pumps it into send_audio(), while relaying stream_audio() output back for playback. Here the backend owns the media bridge. The realtime camera example demonstrates this setup end to end; a minimal FastAPI relay — the browser sends raw PCM16 binary frames and plays the frames it receives — is:

import asyncio

from fastapi import FastAPI, WebSocket

from pydantic_ai import Agent

agent = Agent(instructions='You are a helpful voice assistant.')
app = FastAPI()


@app.websocket('/voice')
async def voice_socket(websocket: WebSocket):
    await websocket.accept()

    async def microphone():
        while True:
            yield await websocket.receive_bytes()

    async with agent.realtime('openai:gpt-realtime-2.1').session() as session:

        async def playback():
            async for chunk in session.stream_audio():
                await websocket.send_bytes(chunk)

        playback_task = asyncio.create_task(playback())
        try:
            await session.send_audio(microphone())
        finally:
            playback_task.cancel()

send_audio() consumes the async iterator for the whole call, so when the browser disconnects, receive_bytes() raises, the finally stops playback, and leaving the async with block hangs up the provider session. Driving the input from a bare asyncio.create_task instead would swallow that error and leave the billed session open with nobody listening.

handle_barge_in=True is a no-op for this relay: played_audio_bytes counts a chunk as played when the relay forwards it, before the browser has actually played it, so the session sees no unplayed audio to flush. The relay must obtain the browser's real playback position, call interrupt(played_bytes=...) with that count, and tell the browser to stop playback and clear its own buffer: the session can only drop what it has not forwarded yet. Passing played_ms= records the provider-side cutoff but never flushes audio queued by the session or buffered in the browser.

items.title: SIP/telephony bridge
items.text: Terminate the phone call with a telephony provider such as Twilio, then build the service that connects its media stream (e.g. Twilio Media Streams over WebSocket) to the backend session, transcoding between the line's codec and PCM16.

items.title: ElevenLabs
items.text:
🌐 এই পেজের সহজ বাংলা সংস্করণ এখনো তৈরি হচ্ছে

আপাতত নিচে মূল ইংরেজি লেখাটি দেখানো হচ্ছে। এই অংশের অন্য পেজগুলোতে সহজ বাংলা ব্যাখ্যা পাবেন।

অফিসিয়াল ইংরেজি পেজ

items.title: ElevenLabs
items.text:
Pydantic AI connects to ElevenLabs in two ways:

  • ElevenLabs Agents runs the conversation on an agent hosted and configured on ElevenAgents, ElevenLabs' agent platform (its voice, LLM, knowledge base, and tools), which Pydantic AI takes over per conversation.
  • Eleven Realtime runs ElevenLabs' speech-to-speech models directly, with the instructions, tools, and history coming from your Pydantic AI agent, as with every other realtime provider.

The difference is where the agent is defined. Use Eleven Realtime unless you need the ElevenAgents platform: your Pydantic AI agent defines the conversation, as it does with any other realtime provider, and a reconnect replays the history.

Use ElevenLabs Agents when the agent lives on the ElevenAgents platform, for its knowledge bases, workflows, and guardrails, or to run a cascaded pipeline with an LLM of your choice. Pydantic AI then overrides the agent's instructions and settings per conversation, and by default checks its client tools against your agent's tools (or syncs them to match; see Configuration ownership). An ElevenAgents agent can also run on an Eleven Realtime model, in Realtime voice mode: that's configured on the agent, and you connect to it through ElevenLabs Agents.

items.title: ElevenLabs Agents
items.text:
Use an elevenlabs-agents:<agent_id> model string, or ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModel for model-level configuration, to connect an agent to the ElevenAgents platform, where the conversation runs on a hosted agent. Start with the realtime quickstart.

ElevenLabs Agents runs a cascaded pipeline (realtime ASR, a configurable LLM, ElevenLabs TTS, and a server-side turn-taking model) behind a pre-provisioned agent, which the conversation reaches over the agent WebSocket. The model wraps that hosted agent, addressed by its agent_id, and Pydantic AI takes ownership of as much of the conversation as ElevenLabs allows per conversation (see Configuration ownership).

items.title: Setup
items.text:
To use ElevenLabs Agents, install pydantic-ai-slim with the elevenlabs-agents-realtime optional group, which bundles the realtime WebSocket transport:

pipuv 
pip install "pydantic-ai-slim[elevenlabs-agents-realtime]"

uv add "pydantic-ai-slim[elevenlabs-agents-realtime]"

Set ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, or pass an ElevenLabsProvider with api_key=. The key is required even for public agents, because the connect-time preflight authenticates with it. The provider's base_url doubles as the region switch: pass a data-residency host such as https://api.eu.residency.elevenlabs.io (or the India and Singapore hosts, api.in.residency.elevenlabs.io and api.sg.residency.elevenlabs.io) to keep both the REST calls and the WebSocket inside a region.

Connecting starts with a REST preflight that fetches the agent: a bad key or an unknown agent id raises a ModelHTTPError from it, and an API that can't be reached raises a RealtimeError. With elevenlabs_agents_tool_sync set to 'error' (the default) or 'off', the key only reads; 'sync' also needs write access to agents and tools.

items.title: Before you connect
items.text:
1. Create the agent in the ElevenLabs dashboard or through the ElevenLabs API, and copy its id.
  2. Under Security > Overrides in the agent's settings, turn on System prompt if the Pydantic AI agent has instructions or a system prompt, plus the toggle of each override setting you use (see Settings).
  3. Under Advanced > Client events, add context_usage, which reports context usage and marks where a spoken response ends (see Usage and cost).
  4. Pick a tool synchronization mode: with the default, 'error', a difference between the session's tools and the agent's client tools fails the connect.

This agent keeps the ElevenLabs agent's client tools in sync with its own:

elevenlabs_agents_tools.py
from pydantic_ai import Agent
from pydantic_ai.realtime.elevenlabs_agents import ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModelSettings

agent = Agent(instructions='You are a friendly concierge. Keep answers short.')


@agent.tool_plain
async def find_restaurant(cuisine: str, party_size: int) -> str:
    """Find a restaurant with a free table.

    Args:
        cuisine: The kind of food the guests want, e.g. 'Italian'.
        party_size: How many guests need a seat.
    """
    return f'Trattoria Roma has a table for {party_size} ({cuisine}).'


realtime_agent = agent.realtime(
    'elevenlabs-agents:agent_0101k2example',
    model_settings=ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModelSettings(elevenlabs_agents_tool_sync='sync'),
)

ElevenLabs needs a description for every tool parameter, which the Args: section of the docstring provides.

items.title: Model names
items.text:
Use elevenlabs-agents:<agent_id> as a model string, for example elevenlabs-agents:agent_0101k2..., or pass the agent id, agent_0101k2..., to ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModel. The agent's own configuration decides the ASR setup, audio formats, turn-taking, and which per-conversation overrides are permitted. Every ModelResponse is stamped with the agent id as its model_name; the LLM the agent runs on is part of the agent configuration and is not reported per response.

That LLM doesn't always answer. When it errors, returns nothing or an invalid tool call, or goes quiet for longer than the agent's prompt.cascade_timeout_seconds (4 seconds by default; in Realtime voice mode, ElevenLabs sets this wait itself), ElevenLabs answers the turn with a backup LLM from its fallback cascade. The response's model_name is still the agent id: only a context_usage report (see Usage and cost) names the LLM, and it isn't tied to a response. The conversations API reports the answering LLM afterwards, per message, as producing_llm. To turn the cascade off, set the agent's prompt.backup_llm_config to {"preference": "disabled"}. To choose the backup LLMs, set it to {"preference": "override", "order": [...]}.

items.title: Configuration ownership
items.text:
Pydantic AI is the source of truth wherever ElevenLabs allows a per-conversation override, and fails loudly where it does not:

  • Instructions: when the Pydantic AI agent defines instructions or a system prompt, the ElevenLabs agent must permit the System prompt override; otherwise the preflight raises a UserError naming the exact toggle. Without local instructions, the ElevenLabs-side prompt is inherited silently.
  • Overrides: first message, language, voice, TTS knobs, the pipeline LLM, and text-only mode are sent in the conversation-initiation override payload. Every override is gated by a per-field toggle under Security > Overrides in the agent's settings (platform_settings.overrides via the API); the preflight checks each override setting against the agent's allowlist before dialing. The raw elevenlabs_agents_config_override escape hatch is the one exception; see Settings.
  • Tools: client tools are workspace entities referenced by the agent, so they cannot be declared inline per conversation. By default the preflight errors when the session's tools and the agent's client tools differ in any way; see Tool synchronization.
  • Stays with the agent: turn-taking and VAD, ASR configuration, audio formats, the voice mode, and platform settings (auth, privacy, guardrails, knowledge bases, workflows).
  • Realtime voice mode: an agent set to a Realtime model (its conversation_config.realtime_model, which can't be overridden per conversation) has ElevenLabs pick the LLM and TTS model. It would ignore elevenlabs_agents_llm and an elevenlabs_agents_tts model_id, so the preflight raises a UserError for either. Every other override works as in Custom mode.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModelSettings — the realtime counterpart of model run settings — extends the shared settings with the agent's per-conversation overrides (greeting, language, voice, TTS delivery, the pipeline LLM), dynamic variables, and the tool synchronization mode:

from pydantic_ai.realtime.elevenlabs_agents import (
    ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModel,
    ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModelSettings,
)

settings = ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModelSettings(
    elevenlabs_agents_voice_id='EXAVITQu4vr4xnSDxMaL',
    elevenlabs_agents_language='de',
    elevenlabs_agents_first_message='Hallo! Wie kann ich helfen?',
    elevenlabs_agents_tts={'stability': 0.4, 'speed': 1.05},
)
model = ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModel('agent_0101k2example', settings=settings)
Setting Purpose elevenlabs_agents_first_message, elevenlabs_agents_language The greeting the agent opens with and the conversation language elevenlabs_agents_voice_id, elevenlabs_agents_tts The provider voice and the TTS delivery knobs (model, stability, speed, similarity boost) elevenlabs_agents_llm The LLM the ElevenLabs pipeline runs, by its ElevenLabs model id elevenlabs_agents_dynamic_variables Values substituted into {{placeholders}} in the agent's prompts and messages elevenlabs_agents_custom_llm_extra_body Extra request body for an agent backed by a custom LLM; gated by its own security toggle elevenlabs_agents_user_id Opaque end-user identifier for ElevenLabs-side analytics elevenlabs_agents_strip_audio_tags Whether expressive audio tags such as [laughs] are removed from the agent's transcripts (True by default); see Provider-specific quirks elevenlabs_agents_tool_sync How the session's tools are reconciled with the agent's client tools; see Tool synchronization elevenlabs_agents_config_override Raw override keys merged last as a forward-compatibility escape hatch

Each elevenlabs_agents_* override setting requires its toggle on the agent, as described above; elevenlabs_agents_dynamic_variables, elevenlabs_agents_user_id, elevenlabs_agents_strip_audio_tags, and elevenlabs_agents_tool_sync need none. elevenlabs_agents_config_override is the one setting deliberately not checked against the permission allowlist — being raw is its point — so a field the agent does not permit there surfaces as the server closing the socket (code 1008, naming the field) after the handshake, not as a local UserError.

Of the shared settings:

  • output_modality='text' maps to the text-only override, toggle-gated like the rest.
  • tool_choice='none' and ToolOrOutput allow-lists restrict the conversation to those tools through the agent's Tool IDs override, toggle-gated like the rest: the agent keeps every tool of the run attached, and the conversation leaves the others out. A choice that forces a tool call ('required', or a list of tool names) raises, as on the other providers.
  • turn_detection cannot be configured: ElevenLabs' server-side turn model is always on, so any value other than True raises. There is no push-to-talk.
  • input_transcription_model=None raises: ASR drives the agent pipeline and cannot be disabled.
  • reconnect raises: a dropped connection ends the session, and a reconnect policy would silently start a conversation that remembers nothing.
  • max_tokens, parallel_tool_calls, async_tool_calls, and thinking have no per-conversation surface and are ignored, matching the shared settings contract.

items.title: Audio formats
items.text:
Audio formats are fixed per agent, not per conversation. The model profile defaults to ElevenLabs' 16 kHz PCM defaults; the connect handshake echoes the agent's actual formats, and the model raises a RealtimeError when they disagree with the profile. For an agent configured differently (e.g. 24 kHz), pass the actual rates via profile=:

from pydantic_ai.realtime.elevenlabs_agents import ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModel

model = ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModel(
    'agent_0101k2example',
    profile={'audio_input_sample_rate': 24000, 'audio_output_sample_rate': 24000},
)

Telephony (ulaw_8000) agents are not supported.

items.title: Tool synchronization
items.text:
elevenlabs_agents_tool_sync controls how the session's ToolDefinitions are reconciled with the agent's client tools at connect time:

  • 'error' (default): raise a UserError describing every difference (missing, extra, or differing tools), so the two can never silently disagree.
  • 'sync': make the workspace match Pydantic AI over REST before dialing: create missing client tools, update differing ones, and re-point the agent's tool_ids, which detaches client tools the run doesn't define (server-side webhook, MCP, and system tools stay attached). A differing tool that another agent also uses isn't changed under it: this agent gets a copy of its own. This mutates workspace state shared by every conversation with the agent, which is why it is opt-in. Treat it as a deploy-time step — a warm-up connect after a tool change — rather than something a customer's first call should pay for: the writes run one after another, and two processes syncing the same agent concurrently race on the final tool_ids re-point, last writer wins. Synced tools get ElevenLabs' default 20-second response timeout (response_timeout_secs); a tool that already has a timeout of its own keeps it when it is updated.
  • 'off': trust the agent's own tool definitions, e.g. for client tools set up on the ElevenLabs side with settings Pydantic AI doesn't sync. A call to a tool the session does not define reaches the tool manager like any other call and is answered with the standard unknown-tool error, which lands in the session's history.

Server-side webhook, MCP, and system tools on the agent are ElevenLabs-owned and never touched, and ElevenLabs runs them itself. Its calls to webhook and system tools (such as end_call) aren't recorded in the session's history; its calls to MCP tools are recorded as a NativeToolCallPart and NativeToolReturnPart. MCP tools that require approval on the ElevenLabs side aren't supported. The session denies such a call (with a warning) rather than leave the conversation waiting up to 300 seconds for an approval that can't come. The agent's LLM is told that the user denied the call, and ElevenLabs reports nothing further about it. Give the agent those tools through a Pydantic AI MCP toolset instead, which is the recommended way, or turn approval off for the tool in the agent's configuration.

ElevenLabs stores tool parameters in its own restricted schema dialect rather than JSON Schema. type, description, enum, items, properties, and required are supported; other keywords (such as additionalProperties or numeric bounds) are not; and every parameter needs a description. Nested models ($defs/$ref) are inlined, and optional (nullable) parameters are collapsed onto their non-null type before conversion, with optionality carried by required alone. The dialect has no way to say null — a required nullable parameter is advertised as its non-null type, and the agent's LLM, which only ever sees the advertised schema, always supplies a value for it. 'sync' therefore fails loudly for a tool whose parameters lack descriptions (add them in the function docstring, and set require_parameter_descriptions=True to catch a missing one when the tool is defined) or use a shape the dialect cannot express (a union of types, or a recursive reference). The 'error' comparison checks what the dialect can express, comparing a parameter's description only when the local schema declares one.

items.title: Feature support and limitations
items.text:
Feature Support Notes Audio format Full feature support Mono PCM16; rates are fixed per agent (16 kHz default) and validated at connect, see Audio formats Text output Limited parameter support output_modality='text' maps to the text-only override, which needs its toggle on the agent Image input Unsupported send() rejects images with a UserError Manual turns Unsupported ElevenLabs' server-side turn model owns turn-taking; turn_detection must stay True Explicit interruption/truncation Unsupported ElevenLabs interrupts server-side and emits RealtimeResponseInterruptedEvent; interrupt() raises Session seeding Unsupported The conversation WebSocket has no history-seeding channel Input transcription Full feature support Always on: per-utterance final transcripts from the agent's ASR; input_transcription_model=None raises Native tools Unsupported None can be configured from the session; configure local fallbacks for web capabilities. The agent's own MCP tool calls are recorded as NativeToolCallParts named mcp_server:<server id> Async tool calls Unsupported The agent waits for each tool result (see concurrent tool execution) Usage Limited parameter support Context tokens only, with context_usage in the agent's client_events; no cost (see Usage and cost) Context window Limited parameter support Known only once the agent reports context_usage: session.context_window_used then gives the share of the LLM's context in use (see Usage and cost) Session duration Limited parameter support Capped by the agent's maximum conversation duration (600 s by default, up to 7,200 s, set on the agent, not per conversation); at the cap the session gets a non-recoverable RealtimeSessionErrorEvent and raises a RealtimeError State-restoring reconnect Unsupported A dropped connection ends the session, and reconnect raises, see Provider session limits

See Audio, images, and transcripts, Turns and interruptions, Tools, and Connection lifecycle for the provider-agnostic workflows.

items.title: Gateway
items.text: ElevenLabs is not currently available through the Pydantic AI Gateway. Connect with an elevenlabs-agents:<agent_id> model string, or with provider='elevenlabs' or an ElevenLabsProvider.

items.title: Usage and cost
items.text:
ElevenLabs reports the LLM's context consumption only, as input_tokens, and only when context_usage is in the agent's conversation.client_events list (it is not by default, and adding it is recommended: it also tells the session where a spoken response ends, see Provider-specific quirks; a session on an agent without it warns once). A report arrives when the agent has finished generating a response, with its last audio chunk (well before that audio has played), and counts toward the session's usage without belonging to any one response. When ElevenLabs answers a turn with a fallback LLM, the report names that model and its context window. The context window it names is kept on ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeConnection.context_limit_tokens, and context_window_used is the ratio of the two.

No price is known for the platform, so usage.cost is always None and a cost_limit can't be enforced. Look the cost up afterwards through the ElevenLabs conversations API: GET /v1/convai/conversations/{conversation_id} reports the conversation's cost in credits as metadata.cost, its length as metadata.call_duration_secs, and a breakdown, including the LLM tokens used per model, under metadata.charging. Every ModelResponse the conversation ends, cut off and lost ones included, carries the conversation's id in provider_details['conversation_id'] (one still under way when the session itself closes has none), and the live connection has it as ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeConnection.conversation_id.

items.title: Provider-specific quirks
items.text:
• In audio mode, a response's transcript arrives whole once the agent's LLM has finished, which can be before or during its audio; only text-only mode streams it. Synthesis outruns playback, so a spoken response is usually delivered in full while the user is still hearing its first words.
  • With a TTS model that voices expressive audio tags, such as eleven_v3_conversational or eleven_v4_turbo, the agent's LLM writes tags like [laughs] into its reply to direct the delivery, and ElevenLabs sends them as part of the response's transcript. Pydantic AI removes them, from the streamed transcript and the one in history alike, and keeps them, in order and without brackets, in the response's provider_details['audio_tags'] (['laughs']). Only lowercase words in square brackets count as tags, so citations ([1]), Markdown links, and placeholders like [Your Name] stay in the text. Set elevenlabs_agents_strip_audio_tags=False to keep the transcript as ElevenLabs sends it ([laughs] Hi there.). To keep the LLM from writing tags in the first place, turn off expressive mode on the agent (tts.expressive_mode: false), which also gives up the expressive delivery. This works only in Custom voice mode: in Realtime voice mode, ElevenLabs manages expressive mode itself.
  • A barge-in cuts each agent message down to what the user heard, as ElevenLabs reports it. Synthesis outruns playback, so this is usually after the message's response has ended. History then holds an interrupted copy of the response, in the same position, whose speech part has the heard text as its transcript: the cut-off message ends in ..., and a message the user heard none of (one after it in the same turn) has no transcript. What the agent said is kept in the part's provider_details['original_transcript']. A response cut off while it is still being generated also carries the heard text in provider_details['corrected_agent_response'].
  • A text turn goes out under an id naming it, and each reply says which text turns it answers (its in_response_to_ids), so wait_for_reply() waits for the reply that answers the text: the one under way, if it names the text, and otherwise the next one. A reply that names a text also answers any text sent before it, as the agent folds text sent while it speaks into one reply, which can name only the latest. (Text sent while the agent speaks usually cuts it off, and the next reply answers it.)
  • send(text, respond=False) is a contextual_update: the agent reads it from its next turn on, without stopping or replying.
  • A response's parallel tool calls each run as soon as they arrive.
  • With elevenlabs_agents_tool_sync='off', client tools registered on the ElevenLabs side with expects_response: false are fire-and-forget: the session still runs them, but their results are never sent back to the agent. (The other modes require every client tool to expect a response.)
  • A conversation waiting in the workspace's concurrency queue hears ElevenLabs' hold audio, which isn't part of the conversation; one that times out there ends with a RealtimeError saying so.

items.title: Eleven Realtime
items.text: Use an elevenlabs:<model> model string, or ElevenLabsRealtimeModel for model-level configuration, to talk to ElevenLabs' Eleven Realtime speech-to-speech models. Unlike ElevenLabs Agents, there is no hosted agent to configure: the session speaks ElevenLabs' OpenAI Realtime-compatible API, and Pydantic AI configures it from your agent. Start with the realtime quickstart.

items.title: Setup
items.text:
To use Eleven Realtime, install pydantic-ai-slim with the elevenlabs-realtime optional group. It includes the openai package, because the API reuses the OpenAI Realtime protocol's event types:

pipuv 
pip install "pydantic-ai-slim[elevenlabs-realtime]"

uv add "pydantic-ai-slim[elevenlabs-realtime]"

Set ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, or pass an ElevenLabsProvider with api_key=. The same key and provider serve ElevenLabs Agents. To keep the connection in a data-residency region, pass the region's host as base_url=:

from pydantic_ai import Agent
from pydantic_ai.providers.elevenlabs import ElevenLabsProvider
from pydantic_ai.realtime.elevenlabs import ElevenLabsRealtimeModel

model = ElevenLabsRealtimeModel(
    'eleven_realtime_v1_mini',
    provider=ElevenLabsProvider(base_url='https://api.eu.residency.elevenlabs.io'),
)
agent = Agent(instructions='You are a friendly voice assistant.')

items.title: Model names
items.text:
Use the elevenlabs: prefix with a model name, e.g. agent.realtime('elevenlabs:eleven_realtime_v1_mini'):

Model Optimized for eleven_realtime_v1_mini Price and latency eleven_realtime_v1_max Quality: it reasons before it responds, for complex instructions and multi-step tool use

eleven_realtime_v1_max needs a max_tokens of at least 1024 (or none), isn't available in the India and Singapore data-residency regions, and costs more per token. See ElevenLabs' model list for the details.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
ElevenLabsRealtimeModelSettings extends the shared settings:

from pydantic_ai.realtime.elevenlabs import ElevenLabsRealtimeModel, ElevenLabsRealtimeModelSettings

settings = ElevenLabsRealtimeModelSettings(
    elevenlabs_voice='george',
    elevenlabs_language='en',
    elevenlabs_max_duration_seconds=1800,
    turn_detection={'sensitivity': 'high'},
)
model = ElevenLabsRealtimeModel('eleven_realtime_v1_mini', settings=settings)
  • elevenlabs_voice takes an ElevenLabs voice ID (e.g. 'JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb') or a default voice's name; the server's default is 'brian'.
  • elevenlabs_language sets the conversation's language (e.g. 'es' or 'pt-br'), which ElevenLabs uses for transcription, speech, and the model's replies. It defaults to English.
  • elevenlabs_max_duration_seconds caps the session's length, from 60 to 7,200 seconds; see Session length.
  • elevenlabs_strip_audio_tags (default True) removes expressive audio tags such as [cheerful] from the model's transcripts, as for ElevenLabs Agents; see Provider-specific quirks.

Turn detection is ElevenLabs' semantic VAD, which decides from what the user said, not only from silence, whether they're done. The shared turn_detection setting maps onto it: sensitivity becomes its eagerness ('low', 'medium', or 'high'), and prefix_padding_ms and silence_duration_ms are passed through. turn_detection=False turns it off for push-to-talk.

The session is configured through the OpenAI Realtime protocol, so ElevenLabsRealtimeModelSettings also takes the OpenAIRealtimeModelSettings fields. openai_turn_detection takes a SemanticVAD, which sets create_response and interrupt_response too; a ServerVAD raises a UserError, as ElevenLabs only supports semantic VAD. ElevenLabs accepts and then ignores the other OpenAI fields, so Pydantic AI doesn't send them: openai_voice (use elevenlabs_voice), openai_input_noise_reduction, openai_output_speed, openai_truncation, and openai_prune_tool_items. Of the shared settings, parallel_tool_calls and thinking are ignored the same way.

Input transcription is always on: each spoken turn's transcript arrives whole once the turn is committed, usually after the reply has started. It takes no model, so input_transcription_model only accepts 'auto' (the default); None still leaves transcripts on, and any other value raises a UserError.

items.title: Feature support and limitations
items.text:
Feature Support Notes Audio format Limited parameter support Mono PCM16 at 24 kHz, input and output. The input rate is configurable (set audio_input_sample_rate through profile=); output is always 24 kHz. The API also offers G.711, which Pydantic AI does not expose Text output Unsupported ElevenLabs answers text input in text, but then ignores audio input altogether, so output_modality='text' raises a UserError Image input Unsupported ElevenLabs drops images from the conversation, so send() rejects them with a UserError before sending Manual turns Full feature support turn_detection=False plus commit/create verbs Interruption Full feature support interrupt() cancels the response, and played_ms truncates what the model remembers saying to what the user heard Session seeding Limited parameter support User and assistant text only; seeded audio and images are unsupported Input transcription Limited parameter support Always on, with whole-turn transcripts; no transcription model to choose Native tools Unsupported ElevenLabs offers MCP tools, which Pydantic AI does not expose yet Async tool calls Unsupported The model answers the user while a tool runs, but then abandons the call, see Provider-specific quirks Usage Unsupported ElevenLabs reports no usage, so token counts are zero and usage.cost is None Reconnection Full feature support Pydantic AI replays completed local history into a new session; in-flight media is lost

See Audio, images, and transcripts, Turns and interruptions, Tools, and Connection lifecycle for the provider-agnostic workflows.

items.title: Browser connections
items.text: ElevenLabs serves OpenAI's client-secret endpoint, but not its WebRTC one, so browser WebRTC isn't available. create_client_secret() still mints the short-lived credential ElevenLabs' own browser guide uses: a browser running OpenAI's Realtime SDK passes it as the API key and opens a WebSocket to wss://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/realtime itself. The secret is bound to the session your agent configures, but the conversation then runs in the browser, outside Pydantic AI.

items.title: Gateway
items.text: Eleven Realtime is not currently available through the Pydantic AI Gateway. Connect with an elevenlabs:<model> model string, or with provider='elevenlabs' or an ElevenLabsProvider.

items.title: Session length
items.text:
ElevenLabs closes a session once it reaches its maximum duration (600 seconds unless elevenlabs_max_duration_seconds says otherwise). With a reconnect policy, the session reconnects, and the new session gets the replayed local history, so the call carries on. Without a reconnect policy, or once its reconnects are used up, the session raises a RealtimeError with ElevenLabs' close reason.

ElevenLabs also closes a session that hasn't received anything from the client for 60 seconds, which happens whenever no microphone audio is streaming, as in a text-only or push-to-talk session. To keep such a session open, the connection sends an empty audio append (which adds no audio) after 45 seconds without sending anything.

items.title: Provider-specific quirks
items.text:
• ElevenLabs' semantic VAD can report that the user stopped speaking, then hear them carry on in the same turn, so RealtimeInputSpeechStartEvent and RealtimeInputSpeechEndEvent can come more than once per turn. The turn joins the history once ElevenLabs commits it.
  • Eleven Realtime writes expressive audio tags such as [cheerful] into its replies to direct the delivery, and sends them as part of the transcript. Pydantic AI removes them, from the streamed transcript and the one in history alike, and keeps them, in order and without brackets, in the response's provider_details['audio_tags'] (['cheerful']). Only lowercase words in square brackets count as tags, so citations ([1]), Markdown links, and placeholders like [Your Name] stay in the text. Set elevenlabs_strip_audio_tags=False to keep the transcript as ElevenLabs sends it.
  • When ElevenLabs replies to something the user said while a tool call is still running, it abandons the call: its result never reaches the model, and a response asked for after it never comes. The session then gets a recoverable RealtimeSessionErrorEvent of type 'tool_calls_abandoned' naming the calls. The tool keeps running and its result is still recorded in history, but no reply to it is waited for: RealtimeTurnCompleteEvent and wait_for_reply() come when the response that cut in ends.
  • ElevenLabs makes parallel tool calls as back-to-back responses of one call each, and answers all their results with one reply, which the session waits for once: RealtimeTurnCompleteEvent and wait_for_reply() come when it ends.
  • eleven_realtime_v1_max sometimes answers a question that needs a tool with two responses: a spoken preamble ("Let me check the weather…") that completes on its own, then the tool call in a response nobody asked for. Nothing links the two, so RealtimeTurnCompleteEvent and wait_for_reply() can come after the preamble, and the tool call and the answer follow as an exchange of their own. History is unaffected. Don't assume the first turn completion after such a question carries the answer: keep consuming the session's events.
  • The protocol follows OpenAI Realtime, but feature support comes from the ElevenLabs model profile; avoid assuming every OpenAI behavior is available.

items.title: Events
items.text:
🌐 এই পেজের সহজ বাংলা সংস্করণ এখনো তৈরি হচ্ছে

আপাতত নিচে মূল ইংরেজি লেখাটি দেখানো হচ্ছে। এই অংশের অন্য পেজগুলোতে সহজ বাংলা ব্যাখ্যা পাবেন।

অফিসিয়াল ইংরেজি পেজ

items.title: Events
items.text:
Iterating a RealtimeSession yields the session's event stream: content parts, tool activity, turn boundaries, reconnects, and recoverable errors. The high-level stream_audio() and stream_transcripts() views described in Audio, images, and transcripts are derived from this same stream, so most applications iterate the session for control flow and leave media to the views.

If nothing is iterating the session, the session keeps the most recent 512 part delta events (audio, transcript, and text) and the most recent 512 structural events for a late async for; older ones are discarded. Discarding a part's start discards the rest of that part with it, so a late iterator never receives a delta it cannot attach to a part. A failure parked for the consumer is never discarded.

items.title: Event reference
items.text:
Event Meaning PartStartEvent A speech, text, or tool part started. PartDeltaEvent Incremental speech audio/transcript or text content. PartEndEvent A finalized part; retained speech audio appears here, not at part start. FunctionToolCallEvent A local function tool began executing. FunctionToolResultEvent A local function tool produced a result — a return, a failure, or a retry. DeferredToolRequestsEvent A tool call was deferred (e.g. needs approval); emitted before any inline capability handler runs. DeferredToolResultsEvent An inline capability handler resolved the deferred requests; the results go through normal tool processing. EnqueuedMessagesEvent Enqueued content was delivered into session history. RealtimeInputSpeechStartEvent The provider detected that the user started speaking, when the profile declares emits_input_speech_events. RealtimeInputSpeechEndEvent The provider detected the end of user speech, when the profile declares emits_input_speech_events. RealtimeResponseInterruptedEvent The provider reported an interrupted model response. RealtimeInputTranscriptionErrorEvent One user turn could not be transcribed; the session remains usable. RealtimeOutputSpeechStartEvent / RealtimeOutputSpeechEndEvent The model became, or stopped being, audible. These are emitted on a gpt-realtime or Azure OpenAI WebRTC sideband, where the provider owns audio playback. RealtimeTurnCompleteEvent The exchange is over: the model gave every reply it owed (or, after a failure, never will), and no tool remains active. RealtimeSessionReconnectEvent The connection was automatically re-established. RealtimeSessionErrorEvent A recoverable provider error occurred; the session remains usable.

A part's index identifies it for the whole session. A provider can finish an output item after a later item has started, so text of the item's transcript can arrive after its part ended: the session then streams that part again under the same index, and the new PartStartEvent replaces the part as it ended. Keep parts by index rather than adding one for every PartEndEvent.

items.title: Shared and realtime-only events
items.text:
The first eight rows are AgentStreamEvent members from pydantic_ai.messages — the same events a standard streamed run yields, so event-handling code written for a text agent (rendering parts, logging tool calls) works on a session unchanged. The Realtime* rows are RealtimeSessionEvent members, the part of AgentStreamEvent that only a session emits: speech detection, interruption, turn completion, reconnection, and recoverable errors have no equivalent in a request-response run.

A capability's event stream hooks see both kinds flow through the same stream; see Capabilities and hooks.

items.title: The turn boundary
items.text:
Use RealtimeTurnCompleteEvent as the exchange boundary. A model can speak, call a tool, and speak again, so receiving speech — or a tool result — does not imply that the turn is done.

The event marks the end of what wait_for_reply() waits for. When a response ends, the session emits it if the model owes nothing more: no reply to anything sent, no answer to a tool's result, and no response still under way.

Only the response that answers an input settles its reply: a response already under way when the input reached the provider never saw it, so it doesn't. Text sent while the model is answering therefore usually gets a reply of its own, and the event comes once that reply ends too. How a provider answers such text varies: GPT-Live speaks to it in the reply it is giving (see OpenAI), and some Gemini Live models cut their reply off for it (see Gemini).

A response the user cuts off by speaking ends the exchange, as does a response the provider started on its own (server-side voice activity detection). The user's transcript can still finish after it.

A tool that raises doesn't end the exchange: the model is told the call failed, and the event comes once it has answered that. An exchange that fails also ends with the event, once: when a tool's result would pass a usage limit, or a failed tool's result can't be sent, the model never gets what it needs to reply. The event follows the exception in the event stream, or comes as the response still under way ends.

items.title: Reading raw audio events
items.text: The audio stream is these events under the hood: stream_audio() is a bounded view over the speech part deltas, and most applications should use it. As an advanced alternative, play SpeechPartDelta.audio_chunk from raw PartDeltaEvents. Model audio arrives in full whether or not history retention is enabled. When output audio is retained, the final SpeechPart contains the whole turn again as a WAV snapshot for history; do not play both or the turn will play twice.

items.title: Google Gemini Live
items.text:
🌐 এই পেজের সহজ বাংলা সংস্করণ এখনো তৈরি হচ্ছে

আপাতত নিচে মূল ইংরেজি লেখাটি দেখানো হচ্ছে। এই অংশের অন্য পেজগুলোতে সহজ বাংলা ব্যাখ্যা পাবেন।

অফিসিয়াল ইংরেজি পেজ

items.title: Google Gemini Live
items.text: GoogleRealtimeModel connects an agent to Gemini Live, including native audio, live images, and provider-native tools. Start with the realtime quickstart or camera example.

items.title: Setup
items.text:
To use Gemini Live models, install pydantic-ai-slim with the google-realtime optional group, which bundles the google-genai SDK together with the realtime transport dependencies:

pipuv 
pip install "pydantic-ai-slim[google-realtime]"

uv add "pydantic-ai-slim[google-realtime]"

Authentication comes from provider, mirroring GoogleModel. Use provider='google' for the Gemini Developer API or provider='google-cloud' for Vertex AI/ADC, with API keys and credentials configured as described in the Google model documentation. Pass a GoogleProvider or GoogleCloudProvider for custom credentials, project, region, or client.

items.title: Model names
items.text:
Use a Gemini Live model ID, for example gemini-3.8-live, gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking, or gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-latest. Live models differ in thinking, asynchronous tools, and output behavior; the profile resolved from the model ID describes what each one supports. Use the official Gemini Live documentation as the canonical model and availability source.

Vertex AI and the Pydantic AI Gateway use different model IDs and locations from the Gemini Developer API:

API Model ID Location Gemini Developer API gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-latest n/a (no location) Gemini Developer API gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview n/a (no location) Gemini Developer API gemini-3.8-live n/a (no location) Gemini Developer API gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking n/a (no location) Vertex AI / gateway gemini-live-2.5-flash global Vertex AI / gateway gemini-live-2.5-flash-native-audio us-central1

The Developer API IDs are not available on Vertex AI. Configure the matching Vertex location on GoogleCloudProvider or in the gateway; the gateway example below uses gemini-live-2.5-flash and therefore requires global.

items.title: Extended thinking
items.text:
gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking reasons in the background while it keeps talking, so it can speak a filler ("Let me check those flights for you"), run a tool, and answer — all within one exchange. It differs from every other Live model in three ways the model handles for you:

  • It requires a thinking level. One is sent even when the session asks for nothing, at the cheapest level the model accepts, because reasoning costs latency. Ask for more with thinking='medium' or 'high'. thinking=False means "as little as possible" here rather than "off", since the model has no off.
  • Its tool calls are always asynchronous. Its profile's async_tool_call_mode is 'always', since the model has no blocking mode, so an explicit async_tool_calls=False is ignored.
  • Its spoken filler doesn't end the turn. Gemini closes the filler's response and says the interaction is still in progress, so the filler and the tool call it was stalling for are recorded as one ModelResponse, and RealtimeTurnCompleteEvent and wait_for_reply() both wait for the model to actually finish. A UI that shows "thinking…" should key off those. An utterance the user barges in on is the exception: it really is over, and is recorded as its own interrupted response.

gemini-3.8-live is the same family without background reasoning. It rejects a thinking level, so the shared thinking setting is ignored rather than sent. Unlike older Live models it defaults to asynchronous tool calls, so Pydantic AI declares tools BLOCKING unless async_tool_calls=True asks otherwise, keeping the same default as every other model.

Both 3.8 models keep proactive audio permanently on, so there's nothing for google_proactive_audio to turn on and it can be left unset. Gemini rejects an explicit False, which Pydantic AI never sends, and True is accepted too. Neither supports affective dialog, and neither does gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview: google_affective_dialog=True raises UserError when the session connects.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
GoogleRealtimeModelSettings — the realtime counterpart of model run settings — extends the shared settings with Google generation and Live controls:

from pydantic_ai.realtime.google import GoogleRealtimeModel, GoogleRealtimeModelSettings

settings = GoogleRealtimeModelSettings(
    temperature=0.7,
    top_p=0.9,
    google_voice='Puck',
    google_language_code='en-US',
    google_affective_dialog=True,
    google_vad={'start_sensitivity': 'high', 'end_sensitivity': 'low'},
    google_turn_coverage='all_video',
    google_context_compression={'trigger_tokens': 16000, 'target_tokens': 8000},
)
model = GoogleRealtimeModel('gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-latest', settings=settings)
Setting Purpose google_voice, google_language_code Voice and output language. A Live session speaks in one voice: the deprecated google_multi_speaker raises when the session connects google_affective_dialog Emotion-aware delivery, on the 2.5 models (not 3.1 Flash Live or the 3.8 models) google_proactive_audio Model-decided speech on native-audio models, served on the Developer API's v1alpha (see below). Always on for the 3.8 models google_vad Exact automatic VAD; fully overrides shared turn_detection google_activity_handling, google_turn_coverage Interruption behavior and which input belongs to a turn google_input_transcription, google_output_transcription Native transcription switches, enabled by default google_context_compression Sliding-window compression for long sessions google_enable_session_resumption Native state restoration; enabled automatically by a reconnect policy google_config_overrides Raw LiveConnectConfig keys merged last as a forward-compatibility escape hatch

google_voice is the provider voice setting. google_thinking_config takes precedence over the shared thinking setting when a token budget or other Gemini-specific control is needed.

google_proactive_audio dials the v1alpha API

Gemini serves proactivity on the Developer API's v1alpha only; on any other version the session is closed with 1007 Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name "proactivity" at 'setup'. When the provider was built from an API key (the default 'google' provider, or GoogleProvider(api_key=...)), a session with google_proactive_audio=True opens its Live connection with a separate v1alpha client built from that key, closed when the session ends. The provider's own client is left as it is, so ordinary GoogleModel requests sharing it keep their version.

A client you built yourself can't be rebuilt that way, so pass one that is already on v1alpha; connecting with one on another version raises UserError:

proactive_audio.py
from google.genai import Client, types

from pydantic_ai.providers.google import GoogleProvider
from pydantic_ai.realtime.google import GoogleRealtimeModel, GoogleRealtimeModelSettings

client = Client(
    api_key='your-api-key', http_options=types.HttpOptions(api_version='v1alpha')
)
model = GoogleRealtimeModel(
    'gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-latest',
    provider=GoogleProvider(client=client),
    settings=GoogleRealtimeModelSettings(google_proactive_audio=True),
)

Unavailable on Vertex AI, whose version line has no v1alpha.

Keep automatic VAD enabled

Pydantic AI does not expose Gemini activity markers or manual turn verbs. Do not set google_vad={'disabled': True}; shared turn_detection=False is rejected for the same reason.

items.title: Asynchronous tool calls
items.text:
Gemini normally pauses generation while a function tool is outstanding. On the native-audio models and gemini-3.8-live, set the shared async_tool_calls setting to True to let it keep speaking and answering: tools are then declared NON_BLOCKING, and their results are returned with INTERRUPT scheduling, so each cuts into whatever the model is saying when it arrives. This is best for slow tools, since a fast result can cut off speech that barely started. What the model says while the tool runs is recorded with the call, ahead of its result: see Transcription and history edge cases.

The other Live models accept a NON_BLOCKING declaration and then wait for the result anyway, so they ignore the setting, and gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking, which has no blocking mode, runs every tool call this way regardless — see Extended thinking. The deprecated google_async_tool_calls setting still works as an alias, with a deprecation warning.

items.title: Native tools
items.text: Gemini Live maps WebSearch to Google Search grounding, the only native tool it supports — no Live model runs native code execution or URL context, so neither CodeExecutionTool nor WebFetch is advertised in supported_native_tools. Give those a local= fallback and the session runs the local tool instead: NativeOrLocalTool(native=CodeExecutionTool(), local=...), or WebFetch(native=False, local=True), which requires the web-fetch optional group (pip/uv-add "pydantic-ai-slim[google-realtime,web-fetch]"). Google Search grounding takes no domain filters or usage limit, so a WebSearch with allowed_domains, blocked_domains, max_uses, or external_web_access=False set fails before the session connects (see restricting parameters).

items.title: Specialist streaming models
items.text:
Gemini also serves specialist streaming models on the same endpoint. The robotics ones, like gemini-robotics-er-2-streaming-preview, are perception models rather than voice assistants: they take in a live audio and video stream and answer in text, for a robot's controller to act on, and reject audio output. Their profile reports supports_audio_output=False, so a session on one asks for text by default and records the answers as TextParts:

robot_perception.py
from pydantic_ai import Agent

perception = Agent(instructions='You are the perception module of a robot.')


async def main(frames=()):
    async with perception.realtime('google:gemini-robotics-er-2-streaming-preview').session() as session:
        for frame in frames:
            await session.send(frame)  # a `BinaryImage` per camera frame
        await session.send('What object is in front of you?')
        await session.wait_for_reply()

For a streaming model the built-in profile doesn't describe, correct the facts with profile=, which resolves like a standard model profile.

items.title: Feature support and limitations
items.text:
Feature Support Notes Audio format Full feature support Mono PCM16, 16 kHz input and 24 kHz output Text output Vertex gemini-live-2.5-flash and the robotics streaming models only The other Live models reject a TEXT response modality, so output_modality='text' raises; read the answer from the transcript on the SpeechPart. The robotics models only write text, which is their default Image/live video input Full feature support Images; google_turn_coverage='all_video' keeps streamed frames in context Manual turns Unsupported Automatic turn detection is required Explicit interruption/truncation Unsupported Gemini interrupts server-side and emits RealtimeResponseInterruptedEvent Input transcription Full feature support Native transcription, enabled by default; no separate model ID Native tools Limited parameter support Google Search grounding only; URL context and code execution fall back to a local= tool (see above) Usage Full feature support Token and modality breakdowns; function-call usage may arrive on a later turn State-restoring reconnect Full feature support Requires session resumption plus a reconnect policy

See Audio, images, and transcripts, Turns and interruptions, Tools, and Connection lifecycle for the provider-agnostic workflows.

items.title: Gateway
items.text:
To route through the Pydantic AI Gateway, use a gateway/-prefixed model string:

from pydantic_ai import Agent

agent = Agent(instructions='You are a helpful voice assistant.')
realtime = agent.realtime('gateway/google:gemini-live-2.5-flash')

The gateway proxies Gemini Live through the Vertex upstream, so configure a region that supports the selected model as listed in Model names. gateway/google-cloud is an alias. See Gateway trace propagation.

items.title: Session resumption
items.text:
For state-restoring reconnects, set the reconnect setting to a ReconnectPolicy; session resumption is enabled automatically alongside it (google_enable_session_resumption can still request handles without a policy, and explicitly setting it to False next to a policy raises UserError rather than silently losing the conversation). Reconnection uses the latest in-memory server handle and emits state_restored=True, unless the drop cut off an exchange the resumed session no longer has (see State restoration).

The connection cap can briefly interrupt a turn

Gemini sends GoAway shortly before its provider-defined connection cap. Pydantic AI reconnects after the drop rather than proactively on GoAway, so a long call can briefly drop mid-turn. This is tracked in #6643.

items.title: Provider-specific quirks
items.text:
• What happens to text (or a tool result) that reaches the model while it generates a reply depends on the model:
  • The native-audio models finish the reply, and answer the text in a turn after it.
  • gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview, gemini-3.8-live, and Vertex's gemini-live-2.5-flash cut the reply off: they emit RealtimeResponseInterruptedEvent, the partial reply is recorded as interrupted, and the next turn answers the text. gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview also cancels the tool calls the cut-off turn was waiting on, and makes them again.

wait_for_reply() and RealtimeTurnCompleteEvent wait for the reply to the text. Where the text went out just as a reply began, before the session saw it start, telling which reply answers the text takes the google_input_cuts_off_reply profile flag: the cut-off reply then answers only what started it. It is on for gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview and gemini-3.8-live, which report where in the audio the user started speaking, telling a reply the user spoke over apart from one text cut off. It is off for Vertex's gemini-live-2.5-flash, which reports no speech, and for the native-audio models, so there a wait for such text can end with the reply already under way. For a model not covered (gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking, say) that cuts its reply off this way and reports speech, turn the flag on with profile=. - Gemini reports response interruption but not user speech-start/end events, so local playback is flushed on RealtimeResponseInterruptedEvent, and Gemini sessions record no user speech span (see Logfire instrumentation). - When Gemini says why it ended a turn, the response records it the way a GoogleModel response does: a malformed function call is finish_reason='error', refused input or unsafe output is 'content_filter', and the raw reason (such as MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL) is kept in provider_details['finish_reason']. - send() sends an image as a live video frame. Spoken turns see video frames, but typed turns don't on the Live models. So a typed turn (send('...')) also carries the most recent image sent in the last 10 seconds in its own content, ahead of the text. That image is sent, and counted as input, twice. Context text (respond=False) and audio don't carry it. To ask about an image in writing, send the two together so the question is always inside the window: session.send([image, 'What is this?']). The google_text_turns_see_video_frames profile flag controls the second send. - Gemini 3.x Live models transcribe the user's speech even with input transcription turned off. Pydantic AI discards those transcripts, so the setting still keeps the user's words out of history, but they are still produced on Google's side. - After resuming from a handle it issued at the start of a turn, gemini-3.8-live can stream that turn's answer without ever sending turn_complete, then answer the next input with RealtimeResponseInterruptedEvent and nothing more. The reply stays open, so wait_for_reply() doesn't return. This happens on Google's side, and no client-side workaround is known. - Native transcription can produce only a completed sentence on some models. Caption UIs should replace text from TranscriptUpdate.transcript rather than assume incremental deltas.

items.title: History and handoff
items.text:
🌐 এই পেজের সহজ বাংলা সংস্করণ এখনো তৈরি হচ্ছে

আপাতত নিচে মূল ইংরেজি লেখাটি দেখানো হচ্ছে। এই অংশের অন্য পেজগুলোতে সহজ বাংলা ব্যাখ্যা পাবেন।

অফিসিয়াল ইংরেজি পেজ

items.title: History and handoff
items.text:
A realtime session builds the same ModelMessage history as a standard agent run — see Messages and chat history. Voice conversations can start from earlier text or voice history, continue in a new realtime session, or hand off to a text model for summarization, extraction, and follow-up.

Spoken turns use SpeechPart; text, images, and tools retain the ordinary ModelRequest and ModelResponse shape.

items.title: Reading session history
items.text:
The session exposes copy-on-read snapshots:

Method Returns all_messages() Seeded history plus messages recorded during this session. new_messages() Only messages recorded during this session.

As in a standard run, a session started without message_history records the agent's system prompts first, as a ModelRequest of SystemPromptParts, so they carry over when the history is handed off or used to seed another session. The model receives them as part of the session instructions.

items.title: Seeding a session
items.text:
Pass message_history= to seed a new session. Replayable text, speech transcripts, thinking text, tool rounds, and supported images are projected into provider conversation items. History processors do not run at seeding; see Capabilities and hooks.

from pydantic_ai import Agent

voice = Agent(instructions='You are a helpful voice assistant.')


async def main(prior_history=()):
    async with voice.realtime(
        'openai:gpt-realtime-2.1',
        message_history=prior_history,
    ).session() as session:
        await session.send('Continue where we left off.')

To continue a text run's conversation, pass its conversation as conversation= instead. It seeds the history and also carries the running usage and the conversation_id, so usage limits keep counting across the handoff and the session correlates with the run in telemetry. Going the other way, session.conversation is the bundle to hand to the next text run.

Seeded tool calls and results are replayed as native function calls where the provider's protocol permits, and as readable text where it doesn't. Thinking signatures and provider-native execution metadata are omitted because they belong to the session that produced them.

Content-less speech parts are skipped because they carry no replayable content. Unsupported content raises UserError instead of being silently dropped. Video, documents, uploaded-file references, and model-generated files cannot be seeded.

Seeded history is trusted

As in a standard run, message_history is treated as trusted server-side state: the system prompt it opens with goes into the session instructions ahead of the agent's own (later system prompts are replayed in place as <system>-tagged text), and its image URLs are downloaded by your server according to the download settings each URL carries. Request-level instructions on seeded history are ignored in favor of the agent's own. If the history came from a browser or another untrusted client, pass it through sanitize_messages before seeding the session; see Loading untrusted history.

Speech transcripts are preferred over retained audio. Where no transcript exists, retained user audio is replayed on models whose profile sets supports_seeding_audio, as long as it was recorded at the model's input sample rate. Assistant speech always needs a transcript for seeding, and an interrupted one is seeded with the same interruption note a text handoff gets, so the model knows the user didn't hear all of it. Check supports_session_seeding, supports_seeding_images, and supports_seeding_audio on the RealtimeModelProfile (see Provider support for how profiles resolve) before constructing portable flows.

items.title: Handing off to a text agent
items.text:
Pass the session snapshot directly to Agent.run():

from pydantic_ai import Agent
from pydantic_ai.realtime import RealtimeTurnCompleteEvent

voice = Agent(instructions='You are a helpful voice assistant.')
notetaker = Agent('openai:gpt-6.1-sol', instructions='Summarize the conversation as bullet points.')


async def main():
    async with voice.realtime('openai:gpt-realtime-2.1').session() as session:
        await session.send('Please remind me to book a train tomorrow.')
        async for event in session:
            if isinstance(event, RealtimeTurnCompleteEvent):
                break

    result = await notetaker.run(
        'Summarize the conversation.', message_history=session.all_messages()
    )
    print(result.output)
    #> - Book a train tomorrow.

Retained user audio is forwarded to standard models whose profile supports audio input; other models receive the transcript. Assistant speech is always handed off as transcript text. Interrupted assistant turns receive a readable interruption note (such as [Interrupted after 1200 ms]) when Pydantic AI prepares the text-model request, and when they are seeded into a realtime session or replayed into one after a reconnect.

For structured work that must finish while the call remains open, expose a delegated text agent as a realtime function tool.

items.title: Context window
items.text:
RealtimeSession.context_window_used reports the fraction of the model's context window in use, and RunContext.context_window_used returns the same value inside a session's tools and hooks. Where the provider reports the fraction itself, the session keeps the latest value; otherwise it is computed as in a standard run, from the latest response's token usage over the model's context_window:

Provider Source OpenAI GPT-Live: reported by Live. gpt-realtime: latest response's total_tokens over the context window, when the window is known Azure OpenAI, Gemini Live Latest response's total_tokens over the context window, when the window is known xAI Grok Voice None: a response's usage counts only the input it added, not the whole conversation ElevenLabs Agents The agent's context_usage report: context_tokens over context_limit_tokens, once per reply, and only with context_usage in the agent's client_events

The value is None until it can be calculated, and it can go down during a session: providers compact or truncate the conversation server-side as it grows, and none of them report when that happens. To control how the provider manages a long conversation, use openai_truncation on OpenAI gpt-realtime and Azure OpenAI or google_context_compression on Gemini. To carry a long conversation on elsewhere, hand it off to a text agent or seed a new session with a summary.

items.title: Retaining audio
items.text:
By default, only transcripts are retained and SpeechPart.audio is None. Pass audio_retention= to session() to retain finalized WAV audio in history:

AudioRetention value Retains 'transcript_only' (default) Transcripts only 'input_audio' User audio 'output_audio' Model audio 'all' Both sides' audio

Retention affects history only. Live input and output remain raw PCM16; finalized retained audio is wrapped in a WAV container.

Retained audio is bounded the same way as retained images. Pass retain_audio_max_seconds= to session() to set how many seconds of audio the session keeps, counting both speakers and the turns still being spoken. It defaults to 1800 (30 minutes, about 86 MB at 24 kHz) and evicts the oldest retained audio when the budget is reached: that turn's SpeechPart keeps its transcript and its audio becomes None, so the history stays valid to hand off or seed a session with. A single turn longer than the budget keeps only its most recent audio. Set it to 0 to retain none or None to remove the bound. Like the image settings, this bounds local history, not provider context: the provider still receives all of the audio. Audio in the message_history you seed a session with is kept as given; the budget covers only the audio the session retains itself. Events the session hasn't delivered to your app yet, such as a queued PartEndEvent or a part waiting in a stream_transcripts() view, keep their part's audio until they are consumed.

Retained audio is kept in the history all_messages() returns, on every provider, and in what is built from it: the conversation a tool sees as RunContext.messages, and the input and output recorded on each response's span.

Input retention follows provider-reported boundaries rather than locally trimming speech. OpenAI gpt-realtime, Azure OpenAI, xAI, and Eleven Realtime normally retain microphone input between reported speech-end boundaries. Gemini Live, GPT-Live, and ElevenLabs Agents don't report those boundaries, so they retain input between response completions. Either form can include silence or other microphone input and should not be treated as a precisely trimmed utterance.

items.title: Retaining images
items.text:
Pass retain_images_every_n= and retain_images_max= to session() to bound how many images stay in local history:

from pydantic_ai import Agent

agent = Agent()


async def main():
    async with agent.realtime('openai:gpt-realtime-2.1').session(
        retain_images_every_n=10, retain_images_max=25
    ):
        ...

These settings bound local history, not provider context: the provider still receives every frame. Images sent through send() are recorded by default; retain_images_every_n=N keeps the first image and then one of every N. retain_images_max defaults to 100 and evicts the oldest retained image when the cap is reached. Set it to 0 to retain none or None to remove the bound.

Sampling controls history growth rate; the maximum provides the actual memory bound. Streaming images continuously approximates live video — the camera example sends one frame per second — so for camera and screen streams, use both deliberately.

items.title: Transcription and history edge cases
items.text:
Input transcription defaults to 'auto'; see Input transcription and each provider page for configuration. Transcripts are recorded with the user turn they describe, even when they arrive after that turn's response or overlap the following turn (on Gemini Live and GPT-Live, until that response ends: see below).

History follows the order of the provider's own conversation:

  • A spoken turn sits where the provider added it, and text, images, and tool results where they reached it. A turn the user started while the model was still answering, but which the provider only committed after that answer ended, is recorded after the answer.
